entry.title: Analysis of Inductor Voltage Formula in RL Charging Circuit Transient
entry.content:
Analysis of Inductor Voltage Formula in RL Charging Circuit Transient

Overview

This comprehensive article provides detailed analysis of the inductor voltage behavior in RL charging circuits during transient conditions. We examine the mathematical relationships between inductor and resistor voltages, the exponential decay characteristics, and the practical implications of inductor voltage changes during the charging process.

RL Charging Circuit Fundamentals

Circuit Configuration

In a typical RL charging circuit:

  • Voltage Source: ( E ) (DC power supply)
  • Resistor: ( R ) (current limiting element)
  • Inductor: ( L ) (energy storage element)
  • Switch: Controls circuit operation
  • Time Constant: ( τ = \frac{L}{R} ) (characteristic charging time)

Charging Process Overview

The charging process involves:

  1. Initial State: Inductor acts as open circuit, no current flow
  2. Current Build-up: Current increases exponentially over time
  3. Voltage Distribution: Voltage gradually transfers from inductor to resistor
  4. Steady State: Current reaches maximum value ( \frac{E}{R} )

Kirchhoff’s Voltage Law Foundation

Circuit Voltage Relationship

According to Kirchhoff’s voltage law, at any time t:
$$ V_L(t) + V_R(t) = E $$

Voltage Distribution Principle

  • Total Voltage: Always equals source voltage E
  • Voltage Transfer: Gradually shifts from inductor to resistor
  • Conservation: Sum of component voltages remains constant

Inductor Voltage Formula Derivation

Method 1: Direct from Kirchhoff’s Law

Using Kirchhoff’s voltage law and the resistor voltage formula:

$$ V_L(t) = E - V_R(t) $$

Substituting the resistor voltage formula:
$$ V_L(t) = E - E(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) $$

Simplifying:
$$ V_L(t) = E - E + E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} = E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

Method 2: From Inductor Current Relationship

Using the inductor voltage-current relationship:
$$ V_L(t) = L \frac{di}{dt} $$

Substituting the current rate of change:
$$ V_L(t) = L \cdot \frac{E}{L} e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} = E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

Final Inductor Voltage Formula

The inductor voltage follows the exponential decay function:

$$ V_L(t) = E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

Formula Parameter Analysis

Parameter Definitions

( E )：Initial inductor voltage at switch closure

  • Physical Meaning: Maximum voltage that appears across the inductor
  • Units: Volts (V)
  • Dependence: Directly proportional to source voltage
  • Initial Value: ( V_L(0) = E )

( t )：Time elapsed after switch closure

  • Physical Meaning: Duration of charging process
  • Units: Seconds (s)
  • Range: ( 0 \leq t < \infty )

( τ = \frac{L}{R} )：Time constant

  • Physical Meaning: Characteristic time for voltage to decay to 36.8% of initial value
  • Units: Seconds (s)
  • Dependence: Proportional to inductance, inversely proportional to resistance

Parameter Relationships

  • Large L: Longer time constant, slower voltage decay
  • Large R: Shorter time constant, faster voltage decay
  • Small L: Shorter time constant, faster voltage decay
  • Small R: Longer time constant, slower voltage decay

Time-Dependent Voltage Behavior

Voltage Decay Characteristics

The inductor voltage exhibits specific behavior patterns:

  1. Initial State: Maximum voltage across inductor
  2. Exponential Decay: Non-linear decrease following exponential function
  3. Asymptotic Approach: Voltage approaches zero as t → ∞
  4. Time Constant Dependence: L/R determines decay rate

Mathematical Analysis

Rate of Change:
$$ \frac{dV_L}{dt} = -\frac{E}{\tau} e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} = -\frac{E}{L/R} e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} = -\frac{ER}{L} e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

Initial Rate:
$$ \frac{dV_L}{dt}\bigg|_{t=0} = -\frac{ER}{L} $$

Key Time Points Analysis

Time Constant Multiples

Important reference points during charging:

1. Initial State (t = 0)

  • Voltage: ( V_L(0) = E ) V
  • Percentage: 100% of initial voltage
  • Behavior: Maximum voltage across inductor

2. One Time Constant (t = τ)

  • Voltage: ( V_L(τ) = E \cdot e^{-1} = 0.368E )
  • Percentage: 36.8% of initial voltage
  • Significance: Standard reference point

3. Two Time Constants (t = 2τ)

  • Voltage: ( V_L(2τ) = E \cdot e^{-2} = 0.135E )
  • Percentage: 13.5% of initial voltage

4. Three Time Constants (t = 3τ)

  • Voltage: ( V_L(3τ) = E \cdot e^{-3} = 0.050E )
  • Percentage: 5.0% of initial voltage

5. Four Time Constants (t = 4τ)

  • Voltage: ( V_L(4τ) = E \cdot e^{-4} = 0.018E )
  • Percentage: 1.8% of initial voltage

6. Five Time Constants (t = 5τ)

  • Voltage: ( V_L(5τ) = E \cdot e^{-5} = 0.007E )
  • Percentage: 0.7% of initial voltage
  • Significance: Transient essentially complete

Voltage Relationships in Circuit

Kirchhoff’s Voltage Law Verification

At any time t:
$$ V_L(t) + V_R(t) = E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} + E(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) = E $$

Component Voltage Relationship

Inductor Voltage:
$$ V_L(t) = E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

Resistor Voltage:
$$ V_R(t) = E(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) $$

Voltage Distribution

  • Initial State: All voltage across inductor
  • Final State: All voltage across resistor
  • Transition: Gradual transfer from inductor to resistor

Exponential Decay Characteristics

Non-Linear Behavior

The inductor voltage follows an exponential decay pattern:

  1. Steep Initial Drop: Rapid voltage decrease at the beginning
  2. Exponential Decay: Non-linear decrease following exponential function
  3. Asymptotic Approach: Voltage approaches zero as t → ∞
  4. Time Constant Dependence: L/R determines decay rate

Mathematical Properties

Decay Rate:

  • Maximum at t = 0
  • Decreases exponentially over time
  • Approaches zero as t → ∞

Curve Shape:

  • Concave downward initially
  • Inflection point at t = τ
  • Becomes more linear as t increases

Sample Calculations

Numerical Example

Given: ( E = 100V ), ( R = 10Ω ), ( L = 0.1H )

Time Constant:

  • ( τ = \frac{L}{R} = \frac{0.1H}{10Ω} = 0.01 ) seconds

At Different Time Points:

Time t/τ V_L V_R Current
0s 0 100V 0V 0A
0.01s 1 36.8V 63.2V 6.32A
0.02s 2 13.5V 86.5V 8.65A
0.03s 3 5.0V 95.0V 9.50A
0.04s 4 1.8V 98.2V 9.82A
0.05s 5 0.7V 99.3V 9.93A

Comparison with RC Charging

Voltage vs Current Behavior

Aspect RL Charging (Inductor Voltage) RC Charging (Resistor Voltage)
Initial Value E 0
Final Value 0 E
Decay Pattern Exponential decrease Exponential increase
Time Constant ( \tau = \frac{L}{R} ) ( \tau = RC )

Energy Considerations

Circuit Type Energy Storage Storage Element
RL Circuit Magnetic energy Inductor
RC Circuit Electric energy Capacitor

Physical Interpretation

Inductor Behavior

  • Initial Opposition: Inductor opposes current change (Lenz’s law)
  • Voltage Generation: Induces voltage to maintain current continuity
  • Energy Storage: Stores energy in magnetic field
  • Gradual Release: Releases energy as current builds up

Voltage Generation Mechanism

  • Self-Induction: Inductor generates voltage to oppose current change
  • Magnetic Field: Voltage proportional to rate of current change
  • Energy Conservation: Energy transfers from electrical to magnetic form

Practical Applications

1. Motor Starting

  • Back EMF: Inductor voltage opposes applied voltage
  • Current Limiting: Controls initial current surge
  • Protection: Prevents excessive starting current

2. Power Electronics

  • DC-DC Converters: Inductor voltage control
  • Switching Regulators: Voltage regulation
  • Filter Design: Voltage smoothing applications

3. Electromagnetic Devices

  • Solenoids: Controlled activation
  • Relays: Gradual current build-up
  • Transformers: Primary voltage control

Common Misconceptions

1. Linear Voltage Decay

  • Misconception: Inductor voltage decreases linearly over time
  • Reality: Voltage follows exponential decay pattern

2. Instant Voltage Disappearance

  • Misconception: Inductor voltage disappears immediately
  • Reality: Voltage decays gradually due to inductor properties

3. Constant Decay Rate

  • Misconception: Voltage decay rate remains constant
  • Reality: Decay rate decreases exponentially over time

4. Energy Loss

  • Misconception: All energy is lost in inductor
  • Reality: Energy is transferred to magnetic field and then to resistor

Problem-Solving Strategy

1. Identify Parameters

  • Extract E, R, L values from problem
  • Calculate time constant ( \tau = \frac{L}{R} )
  • Determine time points of interest

2. Apply Voltage Formula

  • Use ( V_L(t) = E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )
  • Substitute known values
  • Calculate voltage at specified times

3. Verify Results

  • Check units (should be Volts)
  • Ensure voltage decreases from E to 0
  • Verify physical reasonableness

4. Cross-Check Calculations

  • Use Kirchhoff’s voltage law
  • Verify voltage relationships
  • Check time constant calculations

Advanced Topics

Multiple Time Constants

Complex RL scenarios:

  • Series RL: Multiple inductors charging
  • Parallel RL: Multiple charging paths
  • Mixed Configurations: Thevenin equivalent method

Non-Ideal Components

Real-world considerations:

  • Inductor Resistance: Internal resistance effects
  • Core Losses: Magnetic core losses
  • Temperature Effects: Component parameter variations

Reference Video

Title: RL充電電路暫態電感電壓公式解析 - 張偉勤老師
Link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zr6xz1vxyJM

RL充電電路暫態中電感電壓公式解析

概述

本文提供 RL 充電電路中暫態條件下電感電壓行為的詳細分析。我們檢視電感器與電阻電壓之間的數學關係、指數衰減特性，以及充電過程中電感電壓變化的實際影響。

RL充電電路基礎

電路配置

典型的 RL 充電電路包含：

  • 電壓源：( E )（直流電源）
  • 電阻：( R )（限流元件）
  • 電感：( L )（儲能元件）
  • 開關：控制電路操作
  • 時間常數：( τ = \frac{L}{R} )（特徵充電時間）

充電過程概述

充電過程包含：

  1. 初始狀態：電感器呈斷路，無電流流動
  2. 電流建立：電流隨時間指數增長
  3. 電壓分佈：電壓逐漸從電感器轉移到電阻
  4. 穩態：電流達到最大值 ( \frac{E}{R} )

基爾霍夫電壓定律基礎

電路電壓關係

根據基爾霍夫電壓定律，在任何時間 t：
$$ V_L(t) + V_R(t) = E $$

電壓分佈原理

  • 總電壓：始終等於電源電壓 E
  • 電壓轉移：逐漸從電感器轉移到電阻
  • 守恆：元件電壓總和保持恆定

電感電壓公式推導

方法一：直接從基爾霍夫定律

使用基爾霍夫電壓定律和電阻電壓公式：

$$ V_L(t) = E - V_R(t) $$

代入電阻電壓公式：
$$ V_L(t) = E - E(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) $$

簡化：
$$ V_L(t) = E - E + E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} = E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

方法二：從電感電流關係

使用電感電壓電流關係：
$$ V_L(t) = L \frac{di}{dt} $$

代入電流變化率：
$$ V_L(t) = L \cdot \frac{E}{L} e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} = E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

最終電感電壓公式

電感電壓遵循指數衰減函數：

$$ V_L(t) = E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

公式參數分析

參數定義

( E )：開關閉合瞬間電感兩端的初值電壓

  • 物理意義：電感器上出現的最大電壓
  • 單位：伏特（V）
  • 依賴性：與電源電壓成正比
  • 初始值：( V_L(0) = E )

( t )：開關閉合後經過的時間

  • 物理意義：充電過程的持續時間
  • 單位：秒（s）
  • 範圍：( 0 \leq t < \infty )

( τ = \frac{L}{R} )：時間常數

  • 物理意義：電壓衰減到初始值 36.8% 的特徵時間
  • 單位：秒（s）
  • 依賴性：與電感成正比，與電阻成反比

參數關係

  • 大 L：較長時間常數，電壓衰減較慢
  • 大 R：較短時間常數，電壓衰減較快
  • 小 L：較短時間常數，電壓衰減較快
  • 小 R：較長時間常數，電壓衰減較慢

時間相關電壓行為

電壓衰減特性

電感電壓表現出特定的行為模式：

  1. 初始狀態：電感器兩端最大電壓
  2. 指數衰減：非線性減少，遵循指數函數
  3. 漸近接近：當 t → ∞ 時電壓接近零
  4. 時間常數依賴：L/R 決定衰減率

數學分析

變化率：
$$ \frac{dV_L}{dt} = -\frac{E}{\tau} e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} = -\frac{E}{L/R} e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} = -\frac{ER}{L} e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

初始速率：
$$ \frac{dV_L}{dt}\bigg|_{t=0} = -\frac{ER}{L} $$

關鍵時間點分析

時間常數倍數

充電期間的重要參考點：

1. 初始狀態（t = 0）

  • 電壓：( V_L(0) = E ) V
  • 百分比：初始電壓的 100%
  • 行為：電感器兩端最大電壓

2. 一個時間常數（t = τ）

  • 電壓：( V_L(τ) = E \cdot e^{-1} = 0.368E )
  • 百分比：初始電壓的 36.8%
  • 意義：標準參考點

3. 兩個時間常數（t = 2τ）

  • 電壓：( V_L(2τ) = E \cdot e^{-2} = 0.135E )
  • 百分比：初始電壓的 13.5%

4. 三個時間常數（t = 3τ）

  • 電壓：( V_L(3τ) = E \cdot e^{-3} = 0.050E )
  • 百分比：初始電壓的 5.0%

5. 四個時間常數（t = 4τ）

  • 電壓：( V_L(4τ) = E \cdot e^{-4} = 0.018E )
  • 百分比：初始電壓的 1.8%

6. 五個時間常數（t = 5τ）

  • 電壓：( V_L(5τ) = E \cdot e^{-5} = 0.007E )
  • 百分比：初始電壓的 0.7%
  • 意義：暫態基本完成

電路中的電壓關係

基爾霍夫電壓定律驗證

在任何時間 t：
$$ V_L(t) + V_R(t) = E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} + E(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) = E $$

元件電壓關係

電感電壓：
$$ V_L(t) = E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

電阻電壓：
$$ V_R(t) = E(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) $$

電壓分佈

  • 初始狀態：所有電壓在電感器上
  • 最終狀態：所有電壓在電阻上
  • 轉換：從電感器到電阻的逐漸轉移

指數衰減特性

非線性行為

電感電壓遵循指數衰減模式：

  1. 陡峭初始下降：開始時電壓快速減少
  2. 指數衰減：非線性減少，遵循指數函數
  3. 漸近接近：當 t → ∞ 時電壓接近零
  4. 時間常數依賴：L/R 決定衰減率

數學性質

衰減率：

  • 在 t = 0 時最大
  • 隨時間指數衰減
  • 當 t → ∞ 時接近零

曲線形狀：

  • 初始時向下凹
  • 在 t = τ 處有拐點
  • 隨 t 增加變得更線性

計算範例

數值範例

已知： ( E = 100V )，( R = 10Ω )，( L = 0.1H )

時間常數：

  • ( τ = \frac{L}{R} = \frac{0.1H}{10Ω} = 0.01 ) 秒

在不同時間點：

時間 t/τ V_L V_R 電流
0s 0 100V 0V 0A
0.01s 1 36.8V 63.2V 6.32A
0.02s 2 13.5V 86.5V 8.65A
0.03s 3 5.0V 95.0V 9.50A
0.04s 4 1.8V 98.2V 9.82A
0.05s 5 0.7V 99.3V 9.93A

與RC充電比較

電壓與電流行為

方面 RL充電（電感電壓） RC充電（電阻電壓）
初始值 E 0
最終值 0 E
衰減模式 指數減少 指數增加
時間常數 ( \tau = \frac{L}{R} ) ( \tau = RC )

能量考量

電路類型 能量儲存 儲存元件
RL電路 磁能 電感器
RC電路 電能 電容器

物理解釋

電感器行為

  • 初始反對：電感器反對電流變化（楞次定律）
  • 電壓產生：感應電壓以維持電流連續性
  • 能量儲存：在磁場中儲存能量
  • 逐漸釋放：隨電流建立而釋放能量

電壓產生機制

  • 自感應：電感器產生電壓以反對電流變化
  • 磁場：電壓與電流變化率成正比
  • 能量守恆：能量從電能形式轉換為磁能形式

實際應用

1. 電機啟動

  • 反電動勢：電感電壓反對施加電壓
  • 電流限制：控制初始電流湧浪
  • 保護：防止過大的啟動電流

2. 電力電子

  • DC-DC轉換器：電感電壓控制
  • 開關穩壓器：電壓調節
  • 濾波器設計：電壓平滑應用

3. 電磁裝置

  • 螺線管：受控啟動
  • 繼電器：漸進電流建立
  • 變壓器：初級電壓控制

常見誤解

1. 線性電壓衰減

  • 誤解：電感電壓隨時間線性減少
  • 事實：電壓遵循指數衰減模式

2. 瞬間電壓消失

  • 誤解：電感電壓立即消失
  • 事實：由於電感器特性，電壓逐漸衰減

3. 恆定衰減率

  • 誤解：電壓衰減率保持恆定
  • 事實：衰減率隨時間指數衰減

4. 能量損失

  • 誤解：所有能量在電感器中損失
  • 事實：能量轉移到磁場，然後轉移到電阻

解題策略

1. 識別參數

  • 從問題中提取 E、R、L 值
  • 計算時間常數 ( \tau = \frac{L}{R} )
  • 確定感興趣的時間點

2. 應用電壓公式

  • 使用 ( V_L(t) = E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )
  • 代入已知值
  • 計算指定時間的電壓

3. 驗證結果

  • 檢查單位（應為伏特）
  • 確保電壓從 E 減少到 0
  • 驗證物理合理性

4. 交叉檢查計算

  • 使用基爾霍夫電壓定律
  • 驗證電壓關係
  • 檢查時間常數計算

進階主題

多重時間常數

複雜 RL 場景：

  • 串聯 RL：多個電感器充電
  • 並聯 RL：多個充電路徑
  • 混合配置：戴維寧等效法

非理想元件

實際考量：

  • 電感電阻：內部電阻效應
  • 鐵心損耗：磁鐵心損耗
  • 溫度效應：元件參數變化

參考影片

標題： RL充電電路暫態電感電壓公式解析 - 張偉勤老師
連結： https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zr6xz1vxyJM

本文發布日期：2025-08-02

entry.title: Analysis of Resistor Voltage Formula in RL Charging Circuit Transient
entry.content:
Analysis of Resistor Voltage Formula in RL Charging Circuit Transient

Overview

This comprehensive article provides detailed analysis of the resistor voltage behavior in RL charging circuits during transient conditions. We examine the mathematical relationships between current and voltage, the exponential growth characteristics, and the practical implications of resistor voltage changes during inductor charging.

RL Charging Circuit Fundamentals

Circuit Configuration

In a typical RL charging circuit:

  • Voltage Source: ( E ) (DC power supply)
  • Resistor: ( R ) (current limiting element)
  • Inductor: ( L ) (energy storage element)
  • Switch: Controls circuit operation
  • Time Constant: ( τ = \frac{L}{R} ) (characteristic charging time)

Charging Process Overview

The charging process involves:

  1. Initial State: Inductor acts as open circuit, no current flow
  2. Current Build-up: Current increases exponentially over time
  3. Voltage Distribution: Voltage gradually transfers from inductor to resistor
  4. Steady State: Current reaches maximum value ( \frac{E}{R} )

Transient Current Formula Foundation

Current Expression

The current in an RL charging circuit follows the exponential growth function:

$$ i(t) = \frac{E}{R} \left(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}\right) $$

Formula Components

Where:

  • ( i(t) )：Current at time t
  • ( E )：Source voltage
  • ( R )：Resistance value
  • ( t )：Time after switch closure
  • ( τ )：Time constant ( \tau = \frac{L}{R} )

Physical Interpretation

  • Initial Value: ( i(0) = 0 ) A (no current at t = 0)
  • Exponential Growth: Current increases exponentially over time
  • Final Value: ( i(\infty) = \frac{E}{R} ) (steady-state current)
  • Rate Control: Time constant determines growth speed

Resistor Voltage Formula Derivation

Ohm’s Law Application

Using Ohm’s law, the voltage across the resistor is directly proportional to the current:

$$ V_R(t) = i(t) \times R $$

Substitution of Current Formula

Substituting the current formula into Ohm’s law:

$$ V_R(t) = \frac{E}{R} \left(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}\right) \times R $$

Final Resistor Voltage Formula

Simplifying the expression:

$$ V_R(t) = E \left(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}\right) $$

Formula Parameter Analysis

Parameter Definitions

( E )：Final voltage across the resistor (steady-state voltage)

  • Physical Meaning: Maximum voltage that will appear across the resistor
  • Units: Volts (V)
  • Dependence: Directly proportional to source voltage

( t )：Time elapsed after switch closure

  • Physical Meaning: Duration of charging process
  • Units: Seconds (s)
  • Range: ( 0 \leq t < \infty )

( τ = \frac{L}{R} )：Time constant

  • Physical Meaning: Characteristic time for voltage to reach 63.2% of final value
  • Units: Seconds (s)
  • Dependence: Proportional to inductance, inversely proportional to resistance

Parameter Relationships

  • Large L: Longer time constant, slower voltage growth
  • Large R: Shorter time constant, faster voltage growth
  • Small L: Shorter time constant, faster voltage growth
  • Small R: Longer time constant, slower voltage growth

Time-Dependent Voltage Behavior

Voltage Growth Characteristics

The resistor voltage exhibits specific behavior patterns:

  1. Initial State: Zero voltage across resistor
  2. Exponential Growth: Non-linear increase following exponential function
  3. Asymptotic Approach: Voltage approaches final value as t → ∞
  4. Time Constant Dependence: L/R determines growth rate

Mathematical Analysis

Rate of Change:
$$ \frac{dV_R}{dt} = \frac{E}{\tau} e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} = \frac{E}{L/R} e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} = \frac{ER}{L} e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

Initial Rate:
$$ \frac{dV_R}{dt}\bigg|_{t=0} = \frac{ER}{L} $$

Key Time Points Analysis

Time Constant Multiples

Important reference points during charging:

1. Initial State (t = 0)

  • Voltage: ( V_R(0) = 0 ) V
  • Percentage: 0% of final voltage
  • Behavior: No current flow, no voltage drop

2. One Time Constant (t = τ)

  • Voltage: ( V_R(τ) = E(1 - e^{-1}) = 0.632E )
  • Percentage: 63.2% of final voltage
  • Significance: Standard reference point

3. Two Time Constants (t = 2τ)

  • Voltage: ( V_R(2τ) = E(1 - e^{-2}) = 0.865E )
  • Percentage: 86.5% of final voltage

4. Three Time Constants (t = 3τ)

  • Voltage: ( V_R(3τ) = E(1 - e^{-3}) = 0.950E )
  • Percentage: 95.0% of final voltage

5. Four Time Constants (t = 4τ)

  • Voltage: ( V_R(4τ) = E(1 - e^{-4}) = 0.982E )
  • Percentage: 98.2% of final voltage

6. Five Time Constants (t = 5τ)

  • Voltage: ( V_R(5τ) = E(1 - e^{-5}) = 0.993E )
  • Percentage: 99.3% of final voltage
  • Significance: Charging essentially complete

Voltage Relationships in Circuit

Kirchhoff’s Voltage Law

At any time t:
$$ V_R(t) + V_L(t) = E $$

Component Voltage Relationship

Resistor Voltage:
$$ V_R(t) = E(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) $$

Inductor Voltage:
$$ V_L(t) = E e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

Voltage Distribution

  • Initial State: All voltage across inductor
  • Final State: All voltage across resistor
  • Transition: Gradual transfer from inductor to resistor

Exponential Growth Characteristics

Non-Linear Behavior

The resistor voltage follows an exponential growth pattern:

  1. Steep Initial Rise: Rapid voltage increase at the beginning
  2. Exponential Growth: Non-linear increase following exponential function
  3. Asymptotic Approach: Voltage approaches final value as t → ∞
  4. Time Constant Dependence: L/R determines growth rate

Mathematical Properties

Growth Rate:

  • Maximum at t = 0
  • Decreases exponentially over time
  • Approaches zero as t → ∞

Curve Shape:

  • Concave upward initially
  • Inflection point at t = τ
  • Becomes more linear as t increases

Sample Calculations

Numerical Example

Given: ( E = 100V ), ( R = 10Ω ), ( L = 0.1H )

Time Constant:

  • ( τ = \frac{L}{R} = \frac{0.1H}{10Ω} = 0.01 ) seconds

At Different Time Points:

Time t/τ V_R V_L Current
0s 0 0V 100V 0A
0.01s 1 63.2V 36.8V 6.32A
0.02s 2 86.5V 13.5V 8.65A
0.03s 3 95.0V 5.0V 9.50A
0.04s 4 98.2V 1.8V 9.82A
0.05s 5 99.3V 0.7V 9.93A

Comparison with RC Charging

Voltage vs Current Behavior

Aspect RL Charging (Resistor Voltage) RC Charging (Capacitor Voltage)
Initial Value 0 0
Final Value E E
Growth Pattern Exponential increase Exponential increase
Time Constant ( \tau = \frac{L}{R} ) ( \tau = RC )

Energy Considerations

Circuit Type Energy Storage Storage Element
RL Circuit Magnetic energy Inductor
RC Circuit Electric energy Capacitor

Practical Applications

1. Motor Starting

  • Soft Start: Gradual voltage build-up prevents motor damage
  • Current Limiting: Controls initial current surge
  • Protection: Prevents excessive starting current

2. Power Electronics

  • DC-DC Converters: Inductor current control
  • Switching Regulators: Current ramping control
  • Filter Design: Current smoothing applications

3. Electromagnetic Devices

  • Solenoids: Controlled activation
  • Relays: Gradual current build-up
  • Transformers: Primary current control

Common Misconceptions

1. Linear Voltage Growth

  • Misconception: Resistor voltage increases linearly over time
  • Reality: Voltage follows exponential growth pattern

2. Instant Voltage Appearance

  • Misconception: Voltage appears immediately across resistor
  • Reality: Voltage builds up gradually due to inductor opposition

3. Constant Growth Rate

  • Misconception: Voltage growth rate remains constant
  • Reality: Growth rate decreases exponentially over time

4. Energy Loss

  • Misconception: All energy is lost in resistor
  • Reality: Energy is stored in inductor’s magnetic field

Problem-Solving Strategy

1. Identify Parameters

  • Extract E, R, L values from problem
  • Calculate time constant ( \tau = \frac{L}{R} )
  • Determine time points of interest

2. Apply Voltage Formula

  • Use ( V_R(t) = E(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) )
  • Substitute known values
  • Calculate voltage at specified times

3. Verify Results

  • Check units (should be Volts)
  • Ensure voltage increases from 0 to E
  • Verify physical reasonableness

4. Cross-Check Calculations

  • Use current relationships
  • Verify Kirchhoff’s voltage law
  • Check time constant calculations

Advanced Topics

Multiple Time Constants

Complex RL scenarios:

  • Series RL: Multiple inductors charging
  • Parallel RL: Multiple charging paths
  • Mixed Configurations: Thevenin equivalent method

Non-Ideal Components

Real-world considerations:

  • Inductor Resistance: Internal resistance effects
  • Core Losses: Magnetic core losses
  • Temperature Effects: Component parameter variations

Reference Video

Title: RL充電電路暫態電阻電壓公式解析 - 張偉勤老師
Link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ipk9z7mr3to

RL充電電路暫態電阻電壓公式解析

概述

本文提供 RL 充電電路中暫態條件下電阻電壓行為的詳細分析。我們檢視電流與電壓之間的數學關係、指數增長特性，以及電感器充電期間電阻電壓變化的實際影響。

RL充電電路基礎

電路配置

典型的 RL 充電電路包含：

  • 電壓源：( E )（直流電源）
  • 電阻：( R )（限流元件）
  • 電感：( L )（儲能元件）
  • 開關：控制電路操作
  • 時間常數：( τ = \frac{L}{R} )（特徵充電時間）

充電過程概述

充電過程包含：

  1. 初始狀態：電感器呈斷路，無電流流動
  2. 電流建立：電流隨時間指數增長
  3. 電壓分佈：電壓逐漸從電感器轉移到電阻
  4. 穩態：電流達到最大值 ( \frac{E}{R} )

暫態電流公式基礎

電流表達式

RL 充電電路中的電流遵循指數增長函數：

$$ i(t) = \frac{E}{R} \left(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}\right) $$

公式組成

其中：

  • ( i(t) )：時間 t 時的電流
  • ( E )：電源電壓
  • ( R )：電阻值
  • ( t )：開關閉合後的時間
  • ( τ )：時間常數 ( \tau = \frac{L}{R} )

物理解釋

  • 初始值：( i(0) = 0 ) A（t = 0 時無電流）
  • 指數增長：電流隨時間指數增長
  • 最終值：( i(\infty) = \frac{E}{R} )（穩態電流）
  • 速率控制：時間常數決定增長速度

電阻電壓公式推導

歐姆定律應用

使用歐姆定律，電阻兩端電壓與電流成正比：

$$ V_R(t) = i(t) \times R $$

電流公式代入

將電流公式代入歐姆定律：

$$ V_R(t) = \frac{E}{R} \left(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}\right) \times R $$

最終電阻電壓公式

簡化表達式：

$$ V_R(t) = E \left(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}\right) $$

公式參數分析

參數定義

( E )：電阻兩端的最終電壓（穩態電壓）

  • 物理意義：電阻上將出現的最大電壓
  • 單位：伏特（V）
  • 依賴性：與電源電壓成正比

( t )：開關閉合後經過的時間

  • 物理意義：充電過程的持續時間
  • 單位：秒（s）
  • 範圍：( 0 \leq t < \infty )

( τ = \frac{L}{R} )：時間常數

  • 物理意義：電壓達到最終值 63.2% 的特徵時間
  • 單位：秒（s）
  • 依賴性：與電感成正比，與電阻成反比

參數關係

  • 大 L：較長時間常數，電壓增長較慢
  • 大 R：較短時間常數，電壓增長較快
  • 小 L：較短時間常數，電壓增長較快
  • 小 R：較長時間常數，電壓增長較慢

時間相關電壓行為

電壓增長特性

電阻電壓表現出特定的行為模式：

  1. 初始狀態：電阻兩端零電壓
  2. 指數增長：非線性增加，遵循指數函數
  3. 漸近接近：當 t → ∞ 時電壓接近最終值
  4. 時間常數依賴：L/R 決定增長率

數學分析

變化率：
$$ \frac{dV_R}{dt} = \frac{E}{\tau} e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} = \frac{E}{L/R} e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} = \frac{ER}{L} e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

初始速率：
$$ \frac{dV_R}{dt}\bigg|_{t=0} = \frac{ER}{L} $$

關鍵時間點分析

時間常數倍數

充電期間的重要參考點：

1. 初始狀態（t = 0）

  • 電壓：( V_R(0) = 0 ) V
  • 百分比：最終電壓的 0%
  • 行為：無電流流動，無電壓降

2. 一個時間常數（t = τ）

  • 電壓：( V_R(τ) = E(1 - e^{-1}) = 0.632E )
  • 百分比：最終電壓的 63.2%
  • 意義：標準參考點

3. 兩個時間常數（t = 2τ）

  • 電壓：( V_R(2τ) = E(1 - e^{-2}) = 0.865E )
  • 百分比：最終電壓的 86.5%

4. 三個時間常數（t = 3τ）

  • 電壓：( V_R(3τ) = E(1 - e^{-3}) = 0.950E )
  • 百分比：最終電壓的 95.0%

5. 四個時間常數（t = 4τ）

  • 電壓：( V_R(4τ) = E(1 - e^{-4}) = 0.982E )
  • 百分比：最終電壓的 98.2%

6. 五個時間常數（t = 5τ）

  • 電壓：( V_R(5τ) = E(1 - e^{-5}) = 0.993E )
  • 百分比：最終電壓的 99.3%
  • 意義：充電基本完成

電路中的電壓關係

基爾霍夫電壓定律

在任何時間 t：
$$ V_R(t) + V_L(t) = E $$

元件電壓關係

電阻電壓：
$$ V_R(t) = E(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) $$

電感電壓：
$$ V_L(t) = E e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

電壓分佈

  • 初始狀態：所有電壓在電感器上
  • 最終狀態：所有電壓在電阻上
  • 轉換：從電感器到電阻的逐漸轉移

指數增長特性

非線性行為

電阻電壓遵循指數增長模式：

  1. 陡峭初始上升：開始時電壓快速增加
  2. 指數增長：非線性增加，遵循指數函數
  3. 漸近接近：當 t → ∞ 時電壓接近最終值
  4. 時間常數依賴：L/R 決定增長率

數學性質

增長率：

  • 在 t = 0 時最大
  • 隨時間指數衰減
  • 當 t → ∞ 時接近零

曲線形狀：

  • 初始時向上凹
  • 在 t = τ 處有拐點
  • 隨 t 增加變得更線性

計算範例

數值範例

已知： ( E = 100V )，( R = 10Ω )，( L = 0.1H )

時間常數：

  • ( τ = \frac{L}{R} = \frac{0.1H}{10Ω} = 0.01 ) 秒

在不同時間點：

時間 t/τ V_R V_L 電流
0s 0 0V 100V 0A
0.01s 1 63.2V 36.8V 6.32A
0.02s 2 86.5V 13.5V 8.65A
0.03s 3 95.0V 5.0V 9.50A
0.04s 4 98.2V 1.8V 9.82A
0.05s 5 99.3V 0.7V 9.93A

與RC充電比較

電壓與電流行為

方面 RL充電（電阻電壓） RC充電（電容電壓）
初始值 0 0
最終值 E E
增長模式 指數增加 指數增加
時間常數 ( \tau = \frac{L}{R} ) ( \tau = RC )

能量考量

電路類型 能量儲存 儲存元件
RL電路 磁能 電感器
RC電路 電能 電容器

實際應用

1. 電機啟動

  • 軟啟動：漸進電壓建立防止電機損壞
  • 電流限制：控制初始電流湧浪
  • 保護：防止過大的啟動電流

2. 電力電子

  • DC-DC轉換器：電感電流控制
  • 開關穩壓器：電流斜坡控制
  • 濾波器設計：電流平滑應用

3. 電磁裝置

  • 螺線管：受控啟動
  • 繼電器：漸進電流建立
  • 變壓器：初級電流控制

常見誤解

1. 線性電壓增長

  • 誤解：電阻電壓隨時間線性增加
  • 事實：電壓遵循指數增長模式

2. 瞬間電壓出現

  • 誤解：電壓立即出現在電阻上
  • 事實：由於電感器反對，電壓逐漸建立

3. 恆定增長率

  • 誤解：電壓增長率保持恆定
  • 事實：增長率隨時間指數衰減

4. 能量損失

  • 誤解：所有能量在電阻中損失
  • 事實：能量儲存在電感器的磁場中

解題策略

1. 識別參數

  • 從問題中提取 E、R、L 值
  • 計算時間常數 ( \tau = \frac{L}{R} )
  • 確定感興趣的時間點

2. 應用電壓公式

  • 使用 ( V_R(t) = E(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) )
  • 代入已知值
  • 計算指定時間的電壓

3. 驗證結果

  • 檢查單位（應為伏特）
  • 確保電壓從 0 增加到 E
  • 驗證物理合理性

4. 交叉檢查計算

  • 使用電流關係
  • 驗證基爾霍夫電壓定律
  • 檢查時間常數計算

進階主題

多重時間常數

複雜 RL 場景：

  • 串聯 RL：多個電感器充電
  • 並聯 RL：多個充電路徑
  • 混合配置：戴維寧等效法

非理想元件

實際考量：

  • 電感電阻：內部電阻效應
  • 鐵心損耗：磁鐵心損耗
  • 溫度效應：元件參數變化

參考影片

標題： RL充電電路暫態電阻電壓公式解析 - 張偉勤老師
連結： https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ipk9z7mr3to

本文發布日期：2025-08-02

entry.title: RL Charging Transient Basic Formulas and Example Analysis
entry.content:
RL Charging Transient Basic Formulas and Example Analysis

Overview

This comprehensive article provides detailed analysis of the fundamental formulas governing RL charging transient behavior and their application in practical example problems. We examine the mathematical relationships between current and voltage components, time constant calculations, and step-by-step problem-solving strategies.

RL Charging Circuit Fundamentals

Circuit Configuration

In a typical RL charging circuit:

  • Voltage Source: ( E ) (DC power supply)
  • Resistor: ( R ) (current limiting element)
  • Inductor: ( L ) (energy storage element)
  • Switch: Controls circuit operation
  • Time Constant: ( τ = \frac{L}{R} ) (characteristic charging time)

Charging Process Overview

The charging process involves:

  1. Initial State: Inductor acts as open circuit, no current flow
  2. Current Build-up: Current increases exponentially over time
  3. Voltage Distribution: Voltage gradually transfers from inductor to resistor
  4. Steady State: Current reaches maximum value ( \frac{E}{R} )

Fundamental Formulas

1. RL Charging Transient Current Formula

The current in an RL charging circuit follows the exponential growth function:

$$ i(t) = I_{\infty} \times (1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) $$

Where:

  • ( i(t) )：Current at time t
  • ( I_{\infty} )：Steady-state current ( = \frac{E}{R} )
  • ( t )：Time after switch closure
  • ( τ )：Time constant ( = \frac{L}{R} )

Physical Interpretation:

  • Current rises from 0 to steady-state value over time
  • Exponential growth pattern
  • Rate controlled by time constant

2. Resistor Voltage Formula

The voltage across the resistor follows the same exponential growth pattern:

$$ V_R(t) = V_{\infty} \times (1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) $$

Where:

  • ( V_R(t) )：Resistor voltage at time t
  • ( V_{\infty} )：Steady-state voltage ( = E )
  • ( t )：Time after switch closure
  • ( τ )：Time constant ( = \frac{L}{R} )

Physical Interpretation:

  • Resistor voltage rises from 0 to steady-state value
  • Follows same exponential pattern as current
  • Directly proportional to current (Ohm’s law)

3. Inductor Voltage Formula

The voltage across the inductor follows exponential decay:

$$ V_L(t) = V_0 \times e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

Where:

  • ( V_L(t) )：Inductor voltage at time t
  • ( V_0 )：Initial voltage ( = E )
  • ( t )：Time after switch closure
  • ( τ )：Time constant ( = \frac{L}{R} )

Physical Interpretation:

  • Inductor voltage decays from initial value to 0
  • Exponential decay pattern
  • Opposite behavior to resistor voltage

Time Constant Calculation

Definition

The time constant for RL circuits is:

$$ \tau = \frac{L}{R} $$

Physical Significance

  • Units: Seconds (s)
  • Meaning: Time for current to reach 63.2% of final value
  • Growth Rate: Determines how quickly current builds up
  • Circuit Response: Characterizes the circuit’s transient behavior

Example Calculation

Given: ( L = 60mH ), ( R = 20Ω )

Time Constant:
$$ \tau = \frac{L}{R} = \frac{60mH}{20Ω} = \frac{0.06H}{20Ω} = 0.003s = 3ms $$

Kirchhoff’s Voltage Law Verification

Circuit Equation

At any time t:
$$ V_L(t) + V_R(t) = E $$

Formula Verification

Substituting the formulas:
$$ E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} + E(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) = E $$

Simplifying:
$$ E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} + E - E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} = E $$

This confirms that the formulas satisfy Kirchhoff’s voltage law.

Key Time Points Analysis

Time Constant Multiples

Important reference points during charging:

1. Initial State (t = 0)

  • Current: ( i(0) = 0 ) A
  • Resistor Voltage: ( V_R(0) = 0 ) V
  • Inductor Voltage: ( V_L(0) = E ) V
  • Behavior: Inductor acts as open circuit

2. One Time Constant (t = τ)

  • Current: ( i(τ) = 0.632I_{\infty} )
  • Resistor Voltage: ( V_R(τ) = 0.632E )
  • Inductor Voltage: ( V_L(τ) = 0.368E )
  • Significance: Standard reference point

3. Two Time Constants (t = 2τ)

  • Current: ( i(2τ) = 0.865I_{\infty} )
  • Resistor Voltage: ( V_R(2τ) = 0.865E )
  • Inductor Voltage: ( V_L(2τ) = 0.135E )

4. Three Time Constants (t = 3τ)

  • Current: ( i(3τ) = 0.950I_{\infty} )
  • Resistor Voltage: ( V_R(3τ) = 0.950E )
  • Inductor Voltage: ( V_L(3τ) = 0.050E )

5. Five Time Constants (t = 5τ)

  • Current: ( i(5τ) = 0.993I_{\infty} )
  • Resistor Voltage: ( V_R(5τ) = 0.993E )
  • Inductor Voltage: ( V_L(5τ) = 0.007E )
  • Significance: Charging essentially complete

Example Problem Analysis

Problem Setup

Given: ( E = 100V ), ( R = 20Ω ), ( L = 60mH )

Time Constant:
$$ \tau = \frac{L}{R} = \frac{60mH}{20Ω} = 3ms $$

Steady-State Values:

  • Current: ( I_{\infty} = \frac{E}{R} = \frac{100V}{20Ω} = 5A )
  • Resistor Voltage: ( V_{R\infty} = E = 100V )
  • Inductor Voltage: ( V_{L\infty} = 0V )

Calculations at Different Time Points

At t = 0 (Switch Closure)

  • Current: ( i(0) = 5A \times (1 - e^0) = 0A )
  • Resistor Voltage: ( V_R(0) = 100V \times (1 - e^0) = 0V )
  • Inductor Voltage: ( V_L(0) = 100V \times e^0 = 100V )

At t = 3ms (One Time Constant)

  • Current: ( i(3ms) = 5A \times (1 - e^{-1}) = 3.16A )
  • Resistor Voltage: ( V_R(3ms) = 100V \times (1 - e^{-1}) = 63.2V )
  • Inductor Voltage: ( V_L(3ms) = 100V \times e^{-1} = 36.8V )

At t = 6ms (Two Time Constants)

  • Current: ( i(6ms) = 5A \times (1 - e^{-2}) = 4.33A )
  • Resistor Voltage: ( V_R(6ms) = 100V \times (1 - e^{-2}) = 86.5V )
  • Inductor Voltage: ( V_L(6ms) = 100V \times e^{-2} = 13.5V )

At t = 15ms (Five Time Constants)

  • Current: ( i(15ms) = 5A \times (1 - e^{-5}) = 4.97A )
  • Resistor Voltage: ( V_R(15ms) = 100V \times (1 - e^{-5}) = 99.3V )
  • Inductor Voltage: ( V_L(15ms) = 100V \times e^{-5} = 0.7V )

Problem-Solving Strategy

1. Identify Parameters

  • Extract E, R, L values from problem
  • Calculate time constant ( \tau = \frac{L}{R} )
  • Determine steady-state values
  • Identify time points of interest

2. Apply Fundamental Formulas

  • Current: ( i(t) = I_{\infty} \times (1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) )
  • Resistor Voltage: ( V_R(t) = V_{\infty} \times (1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) )
  • Inductor Voltage: ( V_L(t) = V_0 \times e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )

3. Verify Results

  • Check units (current in Amperes, voltage in Volts)
  • Ensure Kirchhoff’s voltage law is satisfied
  • Verify physical reasonableness
  • Cross-check calculations

4. Cross-Check Calculations

  • Use Ohm’s law: ( V_R(t) = i(t) \times R )
  • Verify Kirchhoff’s voltage law: ( V_L(t) + V_R(t) = E )
  • Check time constant calculations

Comparison with RC Charging

Formula Comparison

Component RL Charging RC Charging
Current ( i(t) = I_{\infty}(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) ) ( i(t) = I_0 e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )
Resistor Voltage ( V_R(t) = V_{\infty}(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) ) ( V_R(t) = V_0 e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )
Storage Element Voltage ( V_L(t) = V_0 e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} ) ( V_C(t) = V_{\infty}(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) )
Time Constant ( \tau = \frac{L}{R} ) ( \tau = RC )

Energy Storage

Circuit Type Energy Storage Storage Element
RL Circuit Magnetic energy Inductor
RC Circuit Electric energy Capacitor

Practical Applications

1. Motor Starting

  • Soft Start: Gradual current build-up prevents motor damage
  • Current Limiting: Controls initial current surge
  • Protection: Prevents excessive starting current

2. Power Electronics

  • DC-DC Converters: Inductor current control
  • Switching Regulators: Current ramping control
  • Filter Design: Current smoothing applications

3. Electromagnetic Devices

  • Solenoids: Controlled activation
  • Relays: Gradual current build-up
  • Transformers: Primary current control

Common Misconceptions

1. Linear Growth

  • Misconception: Current increases linearly over time
  • Reality: Current follows exponential growth pattern

2. Instant Current Flow

  • Misconception: Current flows immediately when switch closes
  • Reality: Current builds up gradually due to inductor opposition

3. Constant Growth Rate

  • Misconception: Current growth rate remains constant
  • Reality: Growth rate decreases exponentially over time

4. Energy Loss

  • Misconception: All energy is lost in resistor
  • Reality: Energy is stored in inductor’s magnetic field

Advanced Topics

Multiple Time Constants

Complex RL scenarios:

  • Series RL: Multiple inductors charging
  • Parallel RL: Multiple charging paths
  • Mixed Configurations: Thevenin equivalent method

Non-Ideal Components

Real-world considerations:

  • Inductor Resistance: Internal resistance effects
  • Core Losses: Magnetic core losses
  • Temperature Effects: Component parameter variations

Reference Video

Title: RL充電暫態基本公式與例題解析 - 張偉勤老師
Link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SIqOJ0BBwlE

RL充電暫態基本公式與例題解析

概述

本文提供 RL 充電暫態行為基本公式的詳細分析及其在實際例題中的應用。我們檢視電流與電壓元件之間的數學關係、時間常數計算，以及逐步解題策略。

RL充電電路基礎

電路配置

典型的 RL 充電電路包含：

  • 電壓源：( E )（直流電源）
  • 電阻：( R )（限流元件）
  • 電感：( L )（儲能元件）
  • 開關：控制電路操作
  • 時間常數：( τ = \frac{L}{R} )（特徵充電時間）

充電過程概述

充電過程包含：

  1. 初始狀態：電感器呈斷路，無電流流動
  2. 電流建立：電流隨時間指數增長
  3. 電壓分佈：電壓逐漸從電感器轉移到電阻
  4. 穩態：電流達到最大值 ( \frac{E}{R} )

基本公式

1. RL充電暫態電流公式

RL 充電電路中的電流遵循指數增長函數：

$$ i(t) = I_{\infty} \times (1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) $$

其中：

  • ( i(t) )：時間 t 時的電流
  • ( I_{\infty} )：穩態電流 ( = \frac{E}{R} )
  • ( t )：開關閉合後的時間
  • ( τ )：時間常數 ( = \frac{L}{R} )

物理解釋：

  • 電流隨時間從 0 增加到穩態值
  • 指數增長模式
  • 速率由時間常數控制

2. 電阻電壓公式

電阻兩端電壓遵循相同的指數增長模式：

$$ V_R(t) = V_{\infty} \times (1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) $$

其中：

  • ( V_R(t) )：時間 t 時的電阻電壓
  • ( V_{\infty} )：穩態電壓 ( = E )
  • ( t )：開關閉合後的時間
  • ( τ )：時間常數 ( = \frac{L}{R} )

物理解釋：

  • 電阻電壓從 0 增加到穩態值
  • 與電流遵循相同的指數模式
  • 與電流成正比（歐姆定律）

3. 電感電壓公式

電感兩端電壓遵循指數衰減：

$$ V_L(t) = V_0 \times e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

其中：

  • ( V_L(t) )：時間 t 時的電感電壓
  • ( V_0 )：初始電壓 ( = E )
  • ( t )：開關閉合後的時間
  • ( τ )：時間常數 ( = \frac{L}{R} )

物理解釋：

  • 電感電壓從初始值衰減到 0
  • 指數衰減模式
  • 與電阻電壓相反的行為

時間常數計算

定義

RL 電路的時間常數為：

$$ \tau = \frac{L}{R} $$

物理意義

  • 單位：秒（s）
  • 意義：電流達到最終值 63.2% 的時間
  • 增長率：決定電流建立的速度
  • 電路響應：表徵電路的暫態行為

計算範例

已知： ( L = 60mH )，( R = 20Ω )

時間常數：
$$ \tau = \frac{L}{R} = \frac{60mH}{20Ω} = \frac{0.06H}{20Ω} = 0.003s = 3ms $$

基爾霍夫電壓定律驗證

電路方程式

在任何時間 t：
$$ V_L(t) + V_R(t) = E $$

公式驗證

代入公式：
$$ E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} + E(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) = E $$

簡化：
$$ E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} + E - E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} = E $$

這確認了公式滿足基爾霍夫電壓定律。

關鍵時間點分析

時間常數倍數

充電期間的重要參考點：

1. 初始狀態（t = 0）

  • 電流：( i(0) = 0 ) A
  • 電阻電壓：( V_R(0) = 0 ) V
  • 電感電壓：( V_L(0) = E ) V
  • 行為：電感器呈斷路

2. 一個時間常數（t = τ）

  • 電流：( i(τ) = 0.632I_{\infty} )
  • 電阻電壓：( V_R(τ) = 0.632E )
  • 電感電壓：( V_L(τ) = 0.368E )
  • 意義：標準參考點

3. 兩個時間常數（t = 2τ）

  • 電流：( i(2τ) = 0.865I_{\infty} )
  • 電阻電壓：( V_R(2τ) = 0.865E )
  • 電感電壓：( V_L(2τ) = 0.135E )

4. 三個時間常數（t = 3τ）

  • 電流：( i(3τ) = 0.950I_{\infty} )
  • 電阻電壓：( V_R(3τ) = 0.950E )
  • 電感電壓：( V_L(3τ) = 0.050E )

5. 五個時間常數（t = 5τ）

  • 電流：( i(5τ) = 0.993I_{\infty} )
  • 電阻電壓：( V_R(5τ) = 0.993E )
  • 電感電壓：( V_L(5τ) = 0.007E )
  • 意義：充電基本完成

例題解析

問題設定

已知： ( E = 100V )，( R = 20Ω )，( L = 60mH )

時間常數：
$$ \tau = \frac{L}{R} = \frac{60mH}{20Ω} = 3ms $$

穩態值：

  • 電流：( I_{\infty} = \frac{E}{R} = \frac{100V}{20Ω} = 5A )
  • 電阻電壓：( V_{R\infty} = E = 100V )
  • 電感電壓：( V_{L\infty} = 0V )

不同時間點的計算

t = 0 時（開關閉合）

  • 電流：( i(0) = 5A \times (1 - e^0) = 0A )
  • 電阻電壓：( V_R(0) = 100V \times (1 - e^0) = 0V )
  • 電感電壓：( V_L(0) = 100V \times e^0 = 100V )

t = 3ms 時（一個時間常數）

  • 電流：( i(3ms) = 5A \times (1 - e^{-1}) = 3.16A )
  • 電阻電壓：( V_R(3ms) = 100V \times (1 - e^{-1}) = 63.2V )
  • 電感電壓：( V_L(3ms) = 100V \times e^{-1} = 36.8V )

t = 6ms 時（兩個時間常數）

  • 電流：( i(6ms) = 5A \times (1 - e^{-2}) = 4.33A )
  • 電阻電壓：( V_R(6ms) = 100V \times (1 - e^{-2}) = 86.5V )
  • 電感電壓：( V_L(6ms) = 100V \times e^{-2} = 13.5V )

t = 15ms 時（五個時間常數）

  • 電流：( i(15ms) = 5A \times (1 - e^{-5}) = 4.97A )
  • 電阻電壓：( V_R(15ms) = 100V \times (1 - e^{-5}) = 99.3V )
  • 電感電壓：( V_L(15ms) = 100V \times e^{-5} = 0.7V )

解題策略

1. 識別參數

  • 從問題中提取 E、R、L 值
  • 計算時間常數 ( \tau = \frac{L}{R} )
  • 確定穩態值
  • 識別感興趣的時間點

2. 應用基本公式

  • 電流：( i(t) = I_{\infty} \times (1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) )
  • 電阻電壓：( V_R(t) = V_{\infty} \times (1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) )
  • 電感電壓：( V_L(t) = V_0 \times e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )

3. 驗證結果

  • 檢查單位（電流為安培，電壓為伏特）
  • 確保基爾霍夫電壓定律得到滿足
  • 驗證物理合理性
  • 交叉檢查計算

4. 交叉檢查計算

  • 使用歐姆定律：( V_R(t) = i(t) \times R )
  • 驗證基爾霍夫電壓定律：( V_L(t) + V_R(t) = E )
  • 檢查時間常數計算

與RC充電比較

公式比較

元件 RL充電 RC充電
電流 ( i(t) = I_{\infty}(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) ) ( i(t) = I_0 e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )
電阻電壓 ( V_R(t) = V_{\infty}(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) ) ( V_R(t) = V_0 e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )
儲能元件電壓 ( V_L(t) = V_0 e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} ) ( V_C(t) = V_{\infty}(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) )
時間常數 ( \tau = \frac{L}{R} ) ( \tau = RC )

能量儲存

電路類型 能量儲存 儲存元件
RL電路 磁能 電感器
RC電路 電能 電容器

實際應用

1. 電機啟動

  • 軟啟動：漸進電流建立防止電機損壞
  • 電流限制：控制初始電流湧浪
  • 保護：防止過大的啟動電流

2. 電力電子

  • DC-DC轉換器：電感電流控制
  • 開關穩壓器：電流斜坡控制
  • 濾波器設計：電流平滑應用

3. 電磁裝置

  • 螺線管：受控啟動
  • 繼電器：漸進電流建立
  • 變壓器：初級電流控制

常見誤解

1. 線性增長

  • 誤解：電流隨時間線性增加
  • 事實：電流遵循指數增長模式

2. 瞬間電流流動

  • 誤解：開關閉合時電流立即流動
  • 事實：由於電感器反對，電流逐漸建立

3. 恆定增長率

  • 誤解：電流增長率保持恆定
  • 事實：增長率隨時間指數衰減

4. 能量損失

  • 誤解：所有能量在電阻中損失
  • 事實：能量儲存在電感器的磁場中

進階主題

多重時間常數

複雜 RL 場景：

  • 串聯 RL：多個電感器充電
  • 並聯 RL：多個充電路徑
  • 混合配置：戴維寧等效法

非理想元件

實際考量：

  • 電感電阻：內部電阻效應
  • 鐵心損耗：磁鐵心損耗
  • 溫度效應：元件參數變化

參考影片

標題： RL充電暫態基本公式與例題解析 - 張偉勤老師
連結： https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SIqOJ0BBwlE

本文發布日期：2025-08-02

entry.title: Analysis of Transient Current Formula in RL Charging Circuit
entry.content:
Analysis of Transient Current Formula in RL Charging Circuit

Overview

This comprehensive article provides detailed analysis of the transient current behavior in RL charging circuits. We examine the mathematical relationships, physical principles, and practical applications of current growth during inductor charging, focusing on the exponential nature of the charging process and its relationship to circuit parameters.

RL Charging Circuit Fundamentals

Circuit Configuration

In a typical RL charging circuit:

  • Voltage Source: ( E ) (DC power supply)
  • Resistor: ( R ) (current limiting element)
  • Inductor: ( L ) (energy storage element)
  • Switch: Controls circuit operation
  • Time Constant: ( τ = \frac{L}{R} ) (characteristic charging time)

Charging Process Overview

The charging process involves:

  1. Initial State: Inductor acts as open circuit, no current flow
  2. Current Build-up: Current increases exponentially over time
  3. Energy Storage: Magnetic energy accumulates in inductor
  4. Steady State: Current reaches maximum value ( \frac{E}{R} )

Initial Conditions Analysis

Switch Closure Moment

When switch S closes at t = 0:

  • Initial Current: ( i(0) = 0 ) A (inductor acts as open circuit)
  • Initial Inductor Voltage: ( V_L(0) = E ) (full source voltage)
  • Initial Resistor Voltage: ( V_R(0) = 0 ) (no current flow)
  • Rate of Change: ( \frac{di}{dt}\bigg|_{t=0} = \frac{E}{L} ) (maximum rate)

Physical Interpretation

  • Inductor Behavior: Initially opposes current change (Lenz’s law)
  • Voltage Distribution: All voltage appears across inductor initially
  • Current Growth: Gradual increase as magnetic field builds up

Kirchhoff’s Voltage Law Analysis

Circuit Equation

According to Kirchhoff’s voltage law:

$$ E = i(t)R + L \frac{di(t)}{dt} $$

Equation Components

Where:

  • ( E )：Source voltage
  • ( i(t)R )：Voltage drop across resistor
  • ( L \frac{di(t)}{dt} )：Induced voltage across inductor
  • ( t )：Time after switch closure

Physical Meaning

  • Source Voltage: Provides energy to the circuit
  • Resistor Voltage: Represents energy dissipation
  • Inductor Voltage: Represents energy storage in magnetic field

Transient Current Formula

Mathematical Expression

The current in an RL charging circuit follows the exponential growth function:

$$ i(t) = \frac{E}{R} \left(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}\right) $$

Formula Components

Where:

  • ( i(t) )：Current at time t
  • ( E )：Source voltage
  • ( R )：Resistance value
  • ( t )：Time after switch closure
  • ( τ )：Time constant ( \tau = \frac{L}{R} )

Physical Interpretation

  • Initial Value: ( i(0) = 0 ) A (no current at t = 0)
  • Exponential Growth: Current increases exponentially over time
  • Final Value: ( i(\infty) = \frac{E}{R} ) (steady-state current)
  • Rate Control: Time constant determines growth speed

Time Constant Analysis

Definition

The time constant for RL circuits is:

$$ \tau = \frac{L}{R} $$

Physical Significance

  • Units: Seconds (s)
  • Meaning: Time for current to reach 63.2% of final value
  • Growth Rate: Determines how quickly current builds up
  • Circuit Response: Characterizes the circuit’s transient behavior

Time Constant Dependence

  • Large L: Longer time constant, slower current growth
  • Large R: Shorter time constant, faster current growth
  • Small L: Shorter time constant, faster current growth
  • Small R: Longer time constant, slower current growth

Time-Dependent Behavior

Current Growth Characteristics

The charging current exhibits specific behavior patterns:

  1. Steep Initial Rise: Rapid current increase at the beginning
  2. Exponential Growth: Non-linear increase following exponential function
  3. Asymptotic Approach: Current approaches final value as t → ∞
  4. Time Constant Dependence: L/R determines growth rate

Mathematical Analysis

Rate of Change:
$$ \frac{di}{dt} = \frac{E}{L} e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

Initial Rate:
$$ \frac{di}{dt}\bigg|_{t=0} = \frac{E}{L} $$

Key Time Points Analysis

Time Constant Multiples

Important reference points during charging:

1. Initial State (t = 0)

  • Current: ( i(0) = 0 ) A
  • Percentage: 0% of final current
  • Behavior: Inductor acts as open circuit

2. One Time Constant (t = τ)

  • Current: ( i(τ) = \frac{E}{R}(1 - e^{-1}) = 0.632 \frac{E}{R} )
  • Percentage: 63.2% of final current
  • Significance: Standard reference point

3. Two Time Constants (t = 2τ)

  • Current: ( i(2τ) = \frac{E}{R}(1 - e^{-2}) = 0.865 \frac{E}{R} )
  • Percentage: 86.5% of final current

4. Three Time Constants (t = 3τ)

  • Current: ( i(3τ) = \frac{E}{R}(1 - e^{-3}) = 0.950 \frac{E}{R} )
  • Percentage: 95.0% of final current

5. Five Time Constants (t = 5τ)

  • Current: ( i(5τ) = \frac{E}{R}(1 - e^{-5}) = 0.993 \frac{E}{R} )
  • Percentage: 99.3% of final current
  • Significance: Charging essentially complete

Voltage Relationships

Kirchhoff’s Voltage Law

At any time t:
$$ V_R(t) + V_L(t) = E $$

Component Voltages

Resistor Voltage:
$$ V_R(t) = i(t)R = E(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) $$

Inductor Voltage:
$$ V_L(t) = L \frac{di}{dt} = E e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

Voltage Behavior

  • Initial State: All voltage across inductor
  • Final State: All voltage across resistor
  • Transition: Gradual transfer from inductor to resistor

Energy Considerations

Energy Transfer Process

  1. Initial State: All energy from source
  2. During Charging: Energy distributed between resistor and inductor
  3. Final State: Energy dissipated in resistor, stored in inductor

Mathematical Relationships

Stored Energy at Time t:
$$ W_L(t) = \frac{1}{2}Li^2(t) = \frac{1}{2}L\left(\frac{E}{R}\right)^2(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}})^2 $$

Dissipated Energy:
$$ W_R(t) = \int_0^t i^2(t)R , dt = \frac{1}{2}L\left(\frac{E}{R}\right)^2(1 - e^{-\frac{2t}{\tau}}) $$

Total Energy:
$$ W_{total} = \frac{1}{2}L\left(\frac{E}{R}\right)^2 $$

Sample Calculations

Numerical Example

Given: ( E = 100V ), ( R = 10Ω ), ( L = 0.1H )

Time Constant:

  • ( τ = \frac{L}{R} = \frac{0.1H}{10Ω} = 0.01 ) seconds

At Different Time Points:

Time t/τ Current V_R V_L
0s 0 0A 0V 100V
0.01s 1 6.32A 63.2V 36.8V
0.02s 2 8.65A 86.5V 13.5V
0.03s 3 9.50A 95.0V 5.0V
0.05s 5 9.93A 99.3V 0.7V

Comparison with RC Charging

Current vs Voltage Behavior

Aspect RL Charging (Current) RC Charging (Voltage)
Initial Value 0 0
Final Value ( \frac{E}{R} ) E
Growth Pattern Exponential increase Exponential increase
Time Constant ( \tau = \frac{L}{R} ) ( \tau = RC )

Energy Storage

Circuit Type Energy Storage Storage Element
RL Circuit Magnetic energy Inductor
RC Circuit Electric energy Capacitor

Practical Applications

1. Motor Starting

  • Soft Start: Gradual current build-up prevents motor damage
  • Current Limiting: Controls initial current surge
  • Protection: Prevents excessive starting current

2. Power Electronics

  • DC-DC Converters: Inductor current control
  • Switching Regulators: Current ramping control
  • Filter Design: Current smoothing applications

3. Electromagnetic Devices

  • Solenoids: Controlled activation
  • Relays: Gradual current build-up
  • Transformers: Primary current control

Common Misconceptions

1. Instant Current Flow

  • Misconception: Current flows immediately when switch closes
  • Reality: Current builds up gradually due to inductor opposition

2. Linear Current Growth

  • Misconception: Current increases linearly over time
  • Reality: Current follows exponential growth pattern

3. Constant Inductor Voltage

  • Misconception: Inductor voltage remains constant
  • Reality: Inductor voltage decreases exponentially

4. Energy Loss

  • Misconception: All energy is lost in resistor
  • Reality: Energy is stored in inductor’s magnetic field

Problem-Solving Strategy

1. Identify Parameters

  • Extract E, R, L values from problem
  • Calculate time constant ( \tau = \frac{L}{R} )
  • Determine time points of interest

2. Apply Current Formula

  • Use ( i(t) = \frac{E}{R}(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) )
  • Substitute known values
  • Calculate current at specified times

3. Verify Results

  • Check units (should be Amperes)
  • Ensure current increases from 0 to ( \frac{E}{R} )
  • Verify physical reasonableness

4. Cross-Check Calculations

  • Use voltage relationships
  • Verify energy conservation
  • Check time constant calculations

Advanced Topics

Multiple Time Constants

Complex RL scenarios:

  • Series RL: Multiple inductors charging
  • Parallel RL: Multiple charging paths
  • Mixed Configurations: Thevenin equivalent method

Non-Ideal Components

Real-world considerations:

  • Inductor Resistance: Internal resistance effects
  • Core Losses: Magnetic core losses
  • Temperature Effects: Component parameter variations

Reference Video

Title: RL充電電路暫態電流公式解析 - 張偉勤老師
Link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qFIEPaQKswY

RL充電電路暫態電流公式解析

概述

本文提供 RL 充電電路中暫態電流行為的詳細分析。我們檢視電感器充電期間電流增長的數學關係、物理原理和實際應用，重點關注充電過程的指數特性和其與電路參數的關係。

RL充電電路基礎

電路配置

典型的 RL 充電電路包含：

  • 電壓源：( E )（直流電源）
  • 電阻：( R )（限流元件）
  • 電感：( L )（儲能元件）
  • 開關：控制電路操作
  • 時間常數：( τ = \frac{L}{R} )（特徵充電時間）

充電過程概述

充電過程包含：

  1. 初始狀態：電感器呈斷路，無電流流動
  2. 電流建立：電流隨時間指數增長
  3. 能量儲存：磁能在電感器中累積
  4. 穩態：電流達到最大值 ( \frac{E}{R} )

初始條件分析

開關閉合瞬間

當開關S在 t = 0 時閉合：

  • 初始電流：( i(0) = 0 ) A（電感器呈斷路）
  • 初始電感電壓：( V_L(0) = E )（全電源電壓）
  • 初始電阻電壓：( V_R(0) = 0 )（無電流流動）
  • 變化率：( \frac{di}{dt}\bigg|_{t=0} = \frac{E}{L} )（最大速率）

物理解釋

  • 電感器行為：初始時反對電流變化（楞次定律）
  • 電壓分佈：初始時所有電壓出現在電感器上
  • 電流增長：隨磁場建立而逐漸增加

基爾霍夫電壓定律分析

電路方程式

根據基爾霍夫電壓定律：

$$ E = i(t)R + L \frac{di(t)}{dt} $$

方程式組成

其中：

  • ( E )：電源電壓
  • ( i(t)R )：電阻兩端電壓降
  • ( L \frac{di(t)}{dt} )：電感器感應電壓
  • ( t )：開關閉合後的時間

物理意義

  • 電源電壓：提供電路能量
  • 電阻電壓：代表能量消耗
  • 電感電壓：代表磁場中的能量儲存

暫態電流公式

數學表達式

RL 充電電路中的電流遵循指數增長函數：

$$ i(t) = \frac{E}{R} \left(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}\right) $$

公式組成

其中：

  • ( i(t) )：時間 t 時的電流
  • ( E )：電源電壓
  • ( R )：電阻值
  • ( t )：開關閉合後的時間
  • ( τ )：時間常數 ( \tau = \frac{L}{R} )

物理解釋

  • 初始值：( i(0) = 0 ) A（t = 0 時無電流）
  • 指數增長：電流隨時間指數增長
  • 最終值：( i(\infty) = \frac{E}{R} )（穩態電流）
  • 速率控制：時間常數決定增長速度

時間常數分析

定義

RL 電路的時間常數為：

$$ \tau = \frac{L}{R} $$

物理意義

  • 單位：秒（s）
  • 意義：電流達到最終值 63.2% 的時間
  • 增長率：決定電流建立的速度
  • 電路響應：表徵電路的暫態行為

時間常數依賴性

  • 大 L：較長時間常數，電流增長較慢
  • 大 R：較短時間常數，電流增長較快
  • 小 L：較短時間常數，電流增長較快
  • 小 R：較長時間常數，電流增長較慢

時間相關行為

電流增長特性

充電電流表現出特定的行為模式：

  1. 陡峭初始上升：開始時電流快速增加
  2. 指數增長：非線性增加，遵循指數函數
  3. 漸近接近：當 t → ∞ 時電流接近最終值
  4. 時間常數依賴：L/R 決定增長率

數學分析

變化率：
$$ \frac{di}{dt} = \frac{E}{L} e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

初始速率：
$$ \frac{di}{dt}\bigg|_{t=0} = \frac{E}{L} $$

關鍵時間點分析

時間常數倍數

充電期間的重要參考點：

1. 初始狀態（t = 0）

  • 電流：( i(0) = 0 ) A
  • 百分比：最終電流的 0%
  • 行為：電感器呈斷路

2. 一個時間常數（t = τ）

  • 電流：( i(τ) = \frac{E}{R}(1 - e^{-1}) = 0.632 \frac{E}{R} )
  • 百分比：最終電流的 63.2%
  • 意義：標準參考點

3. 兩個時間常數（t = 2τ）

  • 電流：( i(2τ) = \frac{E}{R}(1 - e^{-2}) = 0.865 \frac{E}{R} )
  • 百分比：最終電流的 86.5%

4. 三個時間常數（t = 3τ）

  • 電流：( i(3τ) = \frac{E}{R}(1 - e^{-3}) = 0.950 \frac{E}{R} )
  • 百分比：最終電流的 95.0%

5. 五個時間常數（t = 5τ）

  • 電流：( i(5τ) = \frac{E}{R}(1 - e^{-5}) = 0.993 \frac{E}{R} )
  • 百分比：最終電流的 99.3%
  • 意義：充電基本完成

電壓關係

基爾霍夫電壓定律

在任何時間 t：
$$ V_R(t) + V_L(t) = E $$

元件電壓

電阻電壓：
$$ V_R(t) = i(t)R = E(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) $$

電感電壓：
$$ V_L(t) = L \frac{di}{dt} = E e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

電壓行為

  • 初始狀態：所有電壓在電感器上
  • 最終狀態：所有電壓在電阻上
  • 轉換：從電感器到電阻的逐漸轉移

能量考量

能量轉移過程

  1. 初始狀態：所有能量來自電源
  2. 充電期間：能量分佈在電阻和電感器之間
  3. 最終狀態：能量在電阻中消耗，儲存在電感器中

數學關係

時間 t 時的儲存能量：
$$ W_L(t) = \frac{1}{2}Li^2(t) = \frac{1}{2}L\left(\frac{E}{R}\right)^2(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}})^2 $$

消耗能量：
$$ W_R(t) = \int_0^t i^2(t)R , dt = \frac{1}{2}L\left(\frac{E}{R}\right)^2(1 - e^{-\frac{2t}{\tau}}) $$

總能量：
$$ W_{total} = \frac{1}{2}L\left(\frac{E}{R}\right)^2 $$

計算範例

數值範例

已知： ( E = 100V )，( R = 10Ω )，( L = 0.1H )

時間常數：

  • ( τ = \frac{L}{R} = \frac{0.1H}{10Ω} = 0.01 ) 秒

在不同時間點：

時間 t/τ 電流 V_R V_L
0s 0 0A 0V 100V
0.01s 1 6.32A 63.2V 36.8V
0.02s 2 8.65A 86.5V 13.5V
0.03s 3 9.50A 95.0V 5.0V
0.05s 5 9.93A 99.3V 0.7V

與RC充電比較

電流與電壓行為

方面 RL充電（電流） RC充電（電壓）
初始值 0 0
最終值 ( \frac{E}{R} ) E
增長模式 指數增加 指數增加
時間常數 ( \tau = \frac{L}{R} ) ( \tau = RC )

能量儲存

電路類型 能量儲存 儲存元件
RL電路 磁能 電感器
RC電路 電能 電容器

實際應用

1. 電機啟動

  • 軟啟動：漸進電流建立防止電機損壞
  • 電流限制：控制初始電流湧浪
  • 保護：防止過大的啟動電流

2. 電力電子

  • DC-DC轉換器：電感電流控制
  • 開關穩壓器：電流斜坡控制
  • 濾波器設計：電流平滑應用

3. 電磁裝置

  • 螺線管：受控啟動
  • 繼電器：漸進電流建立
  • 變壓器：初級電流控制

常見誤解

1. 瞬間電流流動

  • 誤解：開關閉合時電流立即流動
  • 事實：由於電感器反對，電流逐漸建立

2. 線性電流增長

  • 誤解：電流隨時間線性增加
  • 事實：電流遵循指數增長模式

3. 恆定電感電壓

  • 誤解：電感電壓保持恆定
  • 事實：電感電壓指數衰減

4. 能量損失

  • 誤解：所有能量在電阻中損失
  • 事實：能量儲存在電感器的磁場中

解題策略

1. 識別參數

  • 從問題中提取 E、R、L 值
  • 計算時間常數 ( \tau = \frac{L}{R} )
  • 確定感興趣的時間點

2. 應用電流公式

  • 使用 ( i(t) = \frac{E}{R}(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) )
  • 代入已知值
  • 計算指定時間的電流

3. 驗證結果

  • 檢查單位（應為安培）
  • 確保電流從 0 增加到 ( \frac{E}{R} )
  • 驗證物理合理性

4. 交叉檢查計算

  • 使用電壓關係
  • 驗證能量守恆
  • 檢查時間常數計算

進階主題

多重時間常數

複雜 RL 場景：

  • 串聯 RL：多個電感器充電
  • 並聯 RL：多個充電路徑
  • 混合配置：戴維寧等效法

非理想元件

實際考量：

  • 電感電阻：內部電阻效應
  • 鐵心損耗：磁鐵心損耗
  • 溫度效應：元件參數變化

參考影片

標題： RL充電電路暫態電流公式解析 - 張偉勤老師
連結： https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qFIEPaQKswY

本文發布日期：2025-08-02

entry.title: Advanced Example Analysis of RL Discharge Transient Circuit
entry.content:
Advanced Example Analysis of RL Discharge Transient Circuit

Overview

This comprehensive article provides an advanced example analysis of RL discharge transient circuits. We examine complex circuit configurations, apply superposition theorem, and demonstrate sophisticated problem-solving techniques for RL discharge phenomena.

Advanced RL Discharge Circuit Analysis

Circuit Configuration

Complex RL Discharge Circuit:

  • Inductor: L = 2 H (energy storage element)
  • Resistors: Multiple resistors in series-parallel configuration
  • Switch: Controls transition from steady state to discharge
  • Power Supply: Provides initial energy for charging
  • Multiple Paths: Complex discharge path analysis

Steady State Analysis

Before Switch Closure:

  • Inductor State: Fully charged, behaves as short circuit
  • Voltage Distribution:
    • Inductor voltage: 0V (steady state)
    • Resistor voltages: Distributed according to voltage division
  • Current: Calculated using total voltage and resistance
  • Energy State: Maximum magnetic energy stored

Current Calculation:
$$ I_{steady} = \frac{V_{total}}{R_{total}} = \frac{100V}{5k\Omega} = 20mA $$

Transient Analysis

1. Initial Discharge Conditions

When Switch S Closes:

  • Circuit Reconfiguration: New discharge path established
  • Inductor Behavior: Begins discharging stored energy
  • Initial Current: Maintains pre-closure value (20mA)
  • Voltage Polarity: Reverses compared to charging state

2. Voltage Analysis

Inductor Voltage Calculation:
$$ V_L(0) = I(0) \times R_{discharge} = 20mA \times 4k\Omega = 80V $$

Voltage Polarity:

  • Charging: Positive voltage across inductor
  • Discharging: Negative voltage across inductor (opposite polarity)

3. Time Constant Analysis

Discharge Time Constant:
$$ \tau = \frac{L}{R} = \frac{2H}{4k\Omega} = 0.5ms $$

Physical Interpretation:

  • Fast Discharge: Small time constant indicates rapid energy release
  • High Resistance: Large resistance in discharge path
  • Energy Dissipation: Rapid power transfer to resistors

Mathematical Analysis

1. Current Decay Formula

Exponential Decay Expression:
$$ i(t) = I_0 e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} = 20mA \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{0.5ms}} $$

Formula Components:

  • ( i(t) )：Current at time t
  • ( I_0 )：Initial current (20mA)
  • ( t )：Time after discharge begins
  • ( τ )：Time constant (0.5ms)

2. Voltage Decay Formula

Inductor Voltage:
$$ V_L(t) = V_L(0) e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} = 80V \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{0.5ms}} $$

Resistor Voltage:
$$ V_R(t) = i(t) \times R = 20mA \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{0.5ms}} \times 4k\Omega = 80V \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{0.5ms}} $$

3. Time-Dependent Calculations

At t = 1ms (2τ):
$$ i(1ms) = 20mA \cdot e^{-2} = 20mA \cdot 0.135 = 2.7mA $$

$$ V_L(1ms) = 80V \cdot e^{-2} = 80V \cdot 0.135 = 10.8V $$

Superposition Theorem Application

1. Circuit Decomposition

Original Circuit: Complex RL discharge circuit
Decomposed Circuits:

  • Circuit A: Steady-state current source
  • Circuit B: Discharging inductor

2. Individual Circuit Analysis

Circuit A (Steady State):

  • Current Source: 20mA flowing through 4kΩ resistor
  • Voltage: ( V_A = 20mA \times 4k\Omega = 80V )

Circuit B (Discharge):

  • Inductor Current: Decaying from 20mA
  • Voltage: ( V_B(t) = 80V \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{0.5ms}} )

3. Superposition Result

Switch S Current:
$$ I_S(t) = I_{steady} + i_{discharge}(t) = 20mA + 20mA \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{0.5ms}} $$

At t = 1ms:
$$ I_S(1ms) = 20mA + 2.7mA = 22.7mA $$

Total Current Through Switch:
$$ I_{total} = 100mA - 2.7mA = 97.3mA $$

Energy Considerations

1. Initial Magnetic Energy

Stored Energy:
$$ W_L = \frac{1}{2} L I_0^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 2H \times (20mA)^2 = 0.4mJ $$

2. Power Dissipation

Instantaneous Power:
$$ P_R(t) = i^2(t) R = (20mA)^2 \times 4k\Omega \times e^{-\frac{2t}{\tau}} = 1.6W \times e^{-\frac{2t}{0.5ms}} $$

3. Energy Transfer

Total Energy Dissipated:
$$ W_{total} = \int_0^{\infty} P_R(t) dt = 0.4mJ $$

Verification:
$$ W_{total} = \frac{1}{2} L I_0^2 = 0.4mJ $$

Advanced Circuit Analysis

1. Multiple Time Constants

Complex RL Networks:

  • Series RL: ( \tau = \frac{L_{total}}{R_{total}} )
  • Parallel RL: Multiple decay rates
  • Mixed Configurations: Combination effects

2. Non-Ideal Components

Real-World Considerations:

  • Inductor Resistance: Internal resistance effects
  • Core Losses: Magnetic hysteresis losses
  • Temperature Effects: Component parameter variations
  • Parasitic Elements: Stray capacitance and resistance

3. Frequency Domain Analysis

Laplace Transform Method:

  • Transfer Functions: System response analysis
  • Pole-Zero Analysis: Stability considerations
  • Frequency Response: AC behavior analysis

Problem-Solving Strategy

1. Circuit Analysis Steps

  • Identify: Circuit topology and components
  • Determine: Steady-state conditions before switch closure
  • Calculate: Initial conditions for discharge
  • Apply: Appropriate discharge formulas
  • Use: Superposition theorem for complex circuits

2. Formula Application

  • Current: ( i(t) = I_0 e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )
  • Voltage: ( V_L(t) = V_L(0) e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )
  • Time Constant: ( \tau = \frac{L}{R} )
  • Superposition: ( I_{total} = I_{steady} + i_{discharge}(t) )

3. Results Validation

  • Units Check: Ensure proper units
  • Physical Reasonableness: Verify results make sense
  • Law Verification: Confirm Kirchhoff’s laws
  • Energy Conservation: Check energy balance

Practical Applications

1. Power Electronics

  • DC-DC Converters: Complex inductor discharge in switching circuits
  • Motor Drives: Field winding discharge with multiple paths
  • Inverters: Energy recovery systems with complex topologies
  • Switching Power Supplies: Multi-stage energy transfer

2. Protection Circuits

  • Surge Protection: Complex inductor energy dissipation
  • Circuit Breakers: Arc suppression with multiple discharge paths
  • Snubber Circuits: Voltage spike protection in complex circuits
  • EMI Filters: Multi-stage energy absorption

3. Energy Storage Systems

  • Battery Management: Complex inductor discharge control
  • Supercapacitor Systems: Multi-path energy transfer optimization
  • Flywheel Systems: Kinetic energy conversion with multiple stages
  • Magnetic Energy Storage: Complex discharge rate control

Comparison with Simple RL Circuits

Complexity Differences

Aspect Simple RL Circuit Advanced RL Circuit
Configuration Single inductor-resistor Multiple components
Analysis Method Direct formula application Superposition theorem
Time Constants Single time constant Multiple time constants
Energy Paths Single discharge path Multiple discharge paths

Analysis Complexity

Simple RL Circuit:

  • Direct Application: Use basic formulas directly
  • Single Path: One discharge path
  • Single Time Constant: Simple exponential decay

Advanced RL Circuit:

  • Superposition: Decompose into simpler circuits
  • Multiple Paths: Complex discharge paths
  • Multiple Effects: Combined transient responses

Advanced Mathematical Techniques

1. Differential Equations

First-Order RL Circuit:
$$ L \frac{di(t)}{dt} + Ri(t) = 0 $$

Solution Method:
$$ i(t) = I_0 e^{-\frac{R}{L}t} = I_0 e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

2. Laplace Transform

Transfer Function:
$$ H(s) = \frac{I(s)}{V(s)} = \frac{1}{Ls + R} $$

Pole Analysis:
$$ s = -\frac{R}{L} = -\frac{1}{\tau} $$

3. State-Space Analysis

State Variables:
$$ x(t) = i(t) $$

State Equation:
$$ \dot{x}(t) = -\frac{R}{L}x(t) $$

Common Challenges and Solutions

Challenge 1: Complex Circuit Topology

Problem: Multiple components and paths
Solution: Use superposition theorem and circuit decomposition

Challenge 2: Multiple Time Constants

Problem: Different decay rates in different parts
Solution: Analyze each path separately and combine results

Challenge 3: Non-Ideal Components

Problem: Real-world component limitations
Solution: Include parasitic elements in analysis

Challenge 4: Energy Distribution

Problem: Energy transfer through multiple paths
Solution: Use energy conservation and power analysis

Reference Video

Title: RL放電電路暫態進階例題解析 - 張偉勤老師
Link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bYfIhkWAKfs

RL放電電路暫態進階例題解析

概述

本文提供 RL 放電電路暫態進階例題的詳細分析。我們檢視複雜電路配置，應用重疊定理，並展示 RL 放電現象的進階解題技巧。

進階 RL 放電電路分析

電路配置

複雜 RL 放電電路：

  • 電感器：L = 2 H（能量儲存元件）
  • 電阻：串並聯配置中的多個電阻
  • 開關：控制從穩態到放電的轉換
  • 電源：為充電提供初始能量
  • 多重路徑：複雜放電路徑分析

穩態分析

開關閉合前：

  • 電感狀態：完全充電，表現為短路
  • 電壓分佈：
    • 電感電壓：0V（穩態）
    • 電阻電壓：根據電壓分配分佈
  • 電流：使用總電壓和電阻計算
  • 能量狀態：最大磁能儲存

電流計算：
$$ I_{steady} = \frac{V_{total}}{R_{total}} = \frac{100V}{5k\Omega} = 20mA $$

暫態分析

1. 初始放電條件

當開關 S 閉合時：

  • 電路重構：建立新的放電路徑
  • 電感行為：開始釋放儲存的能量
  • 初始電流：維持閉合前的值（20mA）
  • 電壓極性：與充電狀態相反

2. 電壓分析

電感電壓計算：
$$ V_L(0) = I(0) \times R_{discharge} = 20mA \times 4k\Omega = 80V $$

電壓極性：

  • 充電：電感兩端正電壓
  • 放電：電感兩端負電壓（相反極性）

3. 時間常數分析

放電時間常數：
$$ \tau = \frac{L}{R} = \frac{2H}{4k\Omega} = 0.5ms $$

物理解釋：

  • 快速放電：小時間常數表示快速能量釋放
  • 高電阻：放電路徑中的大電阻
  • 能量消耗：快速功率轉移到電阻

數學分析

1. 電流衰減公式

指數衰減表達式：
$$ i(t) = I_0 e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} = 20mA \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{0.5ms}} $$

公式組成：

  • ( i(t) )：時間 t 時的電流
  • ( I_0 )：初始電流（20mA）
  • ( t )：放電開始後的時間
  • ( τ )：時間常數（0.5ms）

2. 電壓衰減公式

電感電壓：
$$ V_L(t) = V_L(0) e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} = 80V \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{0.5ms}} $$

電阻電壓：
$$ V_R(t) = i(t) \times R = 20mA \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{0.5ms}} \times 4k\Omega = 80V \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{0.5ms}} $$

3. 時間相關計算

t = 1ms 時（2τ）：
$$ i(1ms) = 20mA \cdot e^{-2} = 20mA \cdot 0.135 = 2.7mA $$

$$ V_L(1ms) = 80V \cdot e^{-2} = 80V \cdot 0.135 = 10.8V $$

重疊定理應用

1. 電路分解

原始電路：複雜 RL 放電電路
分解電路：

  • 電路 A：穩態電流源
  • 電路 B：放電電感

2. 個別電路分析

電路 A（穩態）：

  • 電流源：20mA 流過 4kΩ 電阻
  • 電壓：( V_A = 20mA \times 4k\Omega = 80V )

電路 B（放電）：

  • 電感電流：從 20mA 衰減
  • 電壓：( V_B(t) = 80V \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{0.5ms}} )

3. 重疊結果

開關 S 電流：
$$ I_S(t) = I_{steady} + i_{discharge}(t) = 20mA + 20mA \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{0.5ms}} $$

t = 1ms 時：
$$ I_S(1ms) = 20mA + 2.7mA = 22.7mA $$

開關總電流：
$$ I_{total} = 100mA - 2.7mA = 97.3mA $$

能量考量

1. 初始磁能

儲存能量：
$$ W_L = \frac{1}{2} L I_0^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 2H \times (20mA)^2 = 0.4mJ $$

2. 功率消耗

瞬時功率：
$$ P_R(t) = i^2(t) R = (20mA)^2 \times 4k\Omega \times e^{-\frac{2t}{\tau}} = 1.6W \times e^{-\frac{2t}{0.5ms}} $$

3. 能量轉移

總能量消耗：
$$ W_{total} = \int_0^{\infty} P_R(t) dt = 0.4mJ $$

驗證：
$$ W_{total} = \frac{1}{2} L I_0^2 = 0.4mJ $$

進階電路分析

1. 多重時間常數

複雜 RL 網路：

  • 串聯 RL：( \tau = \frac{L_{total}}{R_{total}} )
  • 並聯 RL：多重衰減速率
  • 混合配置：組合效應

2. 非理想元件

實際考量：

  • 電感電阻：內部電阻效應
  • 鐵心損耗：磁滯損耗
  • 溫度效應：元件參數變化
  • 寄生元件：雜散電容和電阻

3. 頻域分析

拉普拉斯變換方法：

  • 轉移函數：系統響應分析
  • 極零點分析：穩定性考量
  • 頻率響應：交流行為分析

解題策略

1. 電路分析步驟

  • 識別：電路拓撲和元件
  • 確定：開關閉合前的穩態條件
  • 計算：放電的初始條件
  • 應用：適當的放電公式
  • 使用：複雜電路的重疊定理

2. 公式應用

  • 電流：( i(t) = I_0 e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )
  • 電壓：( V_L(t) = V_L(0) e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )
  • 時間常數：( \tau = \frac{L}{R} )
  • 重疊：( I_{total} = I_{steady} + i_{discharge}(t) )

3. 結果驗證

  • 單位檢查：確保正確的單位
  • 物理合理性：驗證結果合理
  • 定律驗證：確認基爾霍夫定律
  • 能量守恆：檢查能量平衡

實際應用

1. 電力電子

  • DC-DC轉換器：開關電路中的複雜電感放電
  • 電機驅動：具有多重路徑的磁場繞組放電
  • 逆變器：複雜拓撲的能量回收系統
  • 開關電源：多級能量轉移

2. 保護電路

  • 突波保護：複雜電感能量消耗
  • 斷路器：具有多重放電路徑的電弧抑制
  • 緩衝電路：複雜電路中的電壓尖峰保護
  • EMI濾波器：多級能量吸收

3. 能量儲存系統

  • 電池管理：複雜電感放電控制
  • 超級電容器系統：多路徑能量轉移優化
  • 飛輪系統：多級動能轉換
  • 磁能儲存：複雜放電速率控制

與簡單 RL 電路比較

複雜度差異

方面 簡單 RL 電路 進階 RL 電路
配置 單一電感電阻 多個元件
分析方法 直接公式應用 重疊定理
時間常數 單一時間常數 多重時間常數
能量路徑 單一放電路徑 多重放電路徑

分析複雜度

簡單 RL 電路：

  • 直接應用：直接使用基本公式
  • 單一路徑：一個放電路徑
  • 單一時間常數：簡單指數衰減

進階 RL 電路：

  • 重疊：分解為更簡單的電路
  • 多重路徑：複雜放電路徑
  • 多重效應：組合暫態響應

進階數學技巧

1. 微分方程式

一階 RL 電路：
$$ L \frac{di(t)}{dt} + Ri(t) = 0 $$

求解方法：
$$ i(t) = I_0 e^{-\frac{R}{L}t} = I_0 e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

2. 拉普拉斯變換

轉移函數：
$$ H(s) = \frac{I(s)}{V(s)} = \frac{1}{Ls + R} $$

極點分析：
$$ s = -\frac{R}{L} = -\frac{1}{\tau} $$

3. 狀態空間分析

狀態變數：
$$ x(t) = i(t) $$

狀態方程式：
$$ \dot{x}(t) = -\frac{R}{L}x(t) $$

常見挑戰和解決方案

挑戰一：複雜電路拓撲

問題：多個元件和路徑
解決方案：使用重疊定理和電路分解

挑戰二：多重時間常數

問題：不同部分的不同衰減速率
解決方案：分別分析每個路徑並組合結果

挑戰三：非理想元件

問題：實際元件限制
解決方案：在分析中包含寄生元件

挑戰四：能量分佈

問題：通過多重路徑的能量轉移
解決方案：使用能量守恆和功率分析

參考影片

標題： RL放電電路暫態進階例題解析 - 張偉勤老師
連結： https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bYfIhkWAKfs

本文發布日期：2025-08-02

entry.title: Analysis of Resistor and Inductor Voltage Formulas in RL Discharge Transient
entry.content:
Analysis of Resistor and Inductor Voltage Formulas in RL Discharge Transient

Overview

This comprehensive article provides detailed analysis of voltage formulas for both resistor and inductor components in RL discharge transient circuits. We examine the mathematical relationships, physical interpretations, and practical applications of exponential decay in RL discharge phenomena.

RL Discharge Circuit Fundamentals

Circuit Configuration

Basic RL Discharge Circuit:

  • Inductor: Stores magnetic energy
  • Resistor: Dissipates energy during discharge
  • Switch: Controls discharge initiation
  • Initial Conditions: Inductor carries initial current

Discharge Process Overview

When the switch is opened in an RL circuit:

  1. Energy Transfer: Magnetic energy stored in inductor transfers to resistor
  2. Current Decay: Current decreases exponentially over time
  3. Voltage Changes: Both inductor and resistor voltages follow exponential decay
  4. Steady State: Circuit reaches zero current and voltage

Mathematical Foundation

Time Constant Definition

The time constant for RL circuits is defined as:

$$ \tau = \frac{L}{R} $$

Physical Interpretation:

  • Units: Seconds (s)
  • Meaning: Time for current to decay to 36.8% of initial value
  • Circuit Behavior: Characterizes discharge rate

Current Decay Formula

The current in an RL discharge circuit follows:

$$ i(t) = I_0 e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

Where:

  • ( i(t) )：Current at time t
  • ( I_0 )：Initial current
  • ( t )：Time after switch opening
  • ( τ )：Time constant ( = \frac{L}{R} )

Resistor Voltage Analysis

Resistor Voltage Formula

The voltage across the resistor during RL discharge is:

$$ V_R(t) = E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

Formula Components:

  • ( V_R(t) )：Resistor voltage at time t
  • ( E )：Initial voltage (same as initial inductor voltage)
  • ( t )：Time after discharge begins
  • ( τ )：Time constant ( = \frac{L}{R} )

Physical Interpretation

Resistor Voltage Characteristics:

  • Initial Value: ( V_R(0) = E ) (maximum voltage)
  • Decay Pattern: Exponential decrease over time
  • Final Value: ( V_R(\infty) = 0 ) (zero voltage at steady state)
  • Energy Dissipation: Power dissipated as heat in resistor

Time-Dependent Behavior

Key Time Points:

  • t = 0: ( V_R(0) = E ) (100% of initial voltage)
  • t = τ: ( V_R(\tau) = 0.368E ) (36.8% of initial voltage)
  • t = 2τ: ( V_R(2\tau) = 0.135E ) (13.5% of initial voltage)
  • t = 3τ: ( V_R(3\tau) = 0.050E ) (5.0% of initial voltage)
  • t = 5τ: ( V_R(5\tau) \approx 0 ) (effectively zero)

Inductor Voltage Analysis

Inductor Voltage Formula

The voltage across the inductor during RL discharge is:

$$ V_L(t) = -E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

Formula Components:

  • ( V_L(t) )：Inductor voltage at time t
  • ( E )：Initial voltage magnitude
  • ( t )：Time after discharge begins
  • ( τ )：Time constant ( = \frac{L}{R} )
  • Negative Sign: Indicates opposite polarity to resistor voltage

Physical Interpretation

Inductor Voltage Characteristics:

  • Initial Value: ( V_L(0) = -E ) (negative of initial voltage)
  • Decay Pattern: Exponential decrease in magnitude
  • Final Value: ( V_L(\infty) = 0 ) (zero voltage at steady state)
  • Polarity: Opposite to resistor voltage to maintain current flow

Polarity Explanation

Why Negative Sign:

  • Lenz’s Law: Inductor opposes change in current
  • Current Direction: During discharge, current decreases
  • Voltage Polarity: Inductor generates voltage to oppose current decrease
  • Energy Conservation: Maintains circuit equilibrium

Voltage Relationship Analysis

Kirchhoff’s Voltage Law Verification

At any time t, the sum of voltages around the loop must equal zero:

$$ V_L(t) + V_R(t) = 0 $$

Substituting Formulas:
$$ -E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} + E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} = 0 $$

This confirms that our formulas satisfy KVL.

Voltage Magnitude Relationship

Equal Magnitudes:

  • Resistor Voltage: ( |V_R(t)| = E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )
  • Inductor Voltage: ( |V_L(t)| = E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )
  • Relationship: ( |V_R(t)| = |V_L(t)| ) at all times

Opposite Polarity:

  • Resistor: Positive voltage drop
  • Inductor: Negative voltage drop
  • Net Effect: Zero total voltage around loop

Energy Considerations

Initial Energy Storage

Magnetic Energy in Inductor:
$$ W_L = \frac{1}{2} L I_0^2 $$

Energy Dissipation

Power Dissipated in Resistor:
$$ P_R(t) = V_R(t) \cdot i(t) = E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} \cdot I_0 e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} = E I_0 e^{-\frac{2t}{\tau}} $$

Total Energy Dissipated

Energy Conservation:
$$ W_{total} = \int_0^{\infty} P_R(t) dt = \frac{1}{2} L I_0^2 $$

This confirms that all stored energy is dissipated in the resistor.

Comparison with RL Charging

Voltage Polarity Comparison

Component Charging Phase Discharging Phase
Resistor Voltage ( V_R(t) = E(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) ) ( V_R(t) = E e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )
Inductor Voltage ( V_L(t) = E e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} ) ( V_L(t) = -E e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )

Current Direction

  • Charging: Current increases from 0 to ( I_{\infty} )
  • Discharging: Current decreases from ( I_0 ) to 0
  • Voltage Polarity: Reverses to maintain proper current direction

Practical Applications

1. Power Electronics

  • DC-DC Converters: Inductor discharge in switching circuits
  • Motor Drives: Field winding discharge
  • Inverters: Energy recovery systems

2. Protection Circuits

  • Surge Protection: Inductor energy dissipation
  • Circuit Breakers: Arc suppression
  • Snubber Circuits: Voltage spike protection

3. Energy Storage Systems

  • Battery Management: Inductor discharge control
  • Supercapacitor Systems: Energy transfer optimization
  • Flywheel Systems: Kinetic energy conversion

Mathematical Properties

Exponential Decay Characteristics

Decay Rate:

  • Rate of Change: ( \frac{dV}{dt} = -\frac{E}{\tau} e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )
  • Initial Rate: ( \frac{dV}{dt}\big|_{t=0} = -\frac{E}{\tau} )
  • Decay Factor: ( e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} ) determines decay speed

Time Constant Effects

Small Time Constant (τ << 1):

  • Fast Discharge: Rapid voltage decay
  • High Power: Large initial power dissipation
  • Short Duration: Quick transient completion

Large Time Constant (τ >> 1):

  • Slow Discharge: Gradual voltage decay
  • Low Power: Small power dissipation
  • Long Duration: Extended transient period

Sample Calculations

Example Problem

Given:

  • Inductor: L = 100 mH
  • Resistor: R = 50 Ω
  • Initial Current: I₀ = 2 A
  • Initial Voltage: E = 100 V

Calculate:

  1. Time constant
  2. Resistor voltage at t = 2τ
  3. Inductor voltage at t = 2τ

Solution

1. Time Constant:
$$ \tau = \frac{L}{R} = \frac{100 \times 10^{-3}}{50} = 2 \times 10^{-3} = 2ms $$

2. Resistor Voltage at t = 2τ:
$$ V_R(2\tau) = E \cdot e^{-\frac{2\tau}{\tau}} = 100 \cdot e^{-2} = 100 \cdot 0.135 = 13.5V $$

3. Inductor Voltage at t = 2τ:
$$ V_L(2\tau) = -E \cdot e^{-\frac{2\tau}{\tau}} = -100 \cdot e^{-2} = -100 \cdot 0.135 = -13.5V $$

Advanced Analysis

Non-Ideal Components

Real-World Considerations:

  • Inductor Resistance: Internal resistance effects
  • Core Losses: Magnetic hysteresis losses
  • Temperature Effects: Component parameter variations

Multiple Time Constants

Complex RL Networks:

  • Series RL: Multiple inductors in series
  • Parallel RL: Multiple inductors in parallel
  • Mixed Configurations: Combination networks

Frequency Domain Analysis

Laplace Transform Method:

  • Transfer Functions: System response analysis
  • Pole-Zero Analysis: Stability considerations
  • Frequency Response: AC behavior analysis

Problem-Solving Strategy

1. Circuit Analysis

  • Identify: Circuit topology and components
  • Determine: Initial conditions
  • Calculate: Time constant τ = L/R
  • Apply: Appropriate voltage formulas

2. Formula Application

  • Resistor Voltage: ( V_R(t) = E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )
  • Inductor Voltage: ( V_L(t) = -E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )
  • Time Points: Calculate at specific times
  • Verification: Check KVL compliance

3. Results Validation

  • Units Check: Ensure proper voltage units
  • Physical Reasonableness: Verify results make sense
  • Law Verification: Confirm Kirchhoff’s laws
  • Energy Conservation: Check energy balance

Common Misconceptions

Misconception 1: Voltage Polarity

Error: Assuming inductor voltage has same polarity as resistor
Correction: Inductor voltage has opposite polarity to maintain current flow

Misconception 2: Energy Loss

Error: Thinking energy is lost during discharge
Correction: Energy is conserved, transferred from inductor to resistor

Misconception 3: Time Constant

Error: Confusing charging and discharging time constants
Correction: Same time constant τ = L/R for both processes

Reference Video

Title: RL放電暫態電阻與電感電壓公式解析 - 張偉勤老師
Link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z2NOmVPGAdw

RL放電暫態電阻與電感電壓公式解析

概述

本文提供 RL 放電暫態電路中電阻和電感元件電壓公式的詳細分析。我們檢視數學關係、物理解釋，以及 RL 放電現象中指數衰減的實際應用。

RL 放電電路基礎

電路配置

基本 RL 放電電路：

  • 電感器：儲存磁能
  • 電阻：放電期間消耗能量
  • 開關：控制放電開始
  • 初始條件：電感器攜帶初始電流

放電過程概述

當 RL 電路中的開關打開時：

  1. 能量轉移：儲存在電感器中的磁能轉移到電阻
  2. 電流衰減：電流隨時間指數衰減
  3. 電壓變化：電感和電阻電壓都遵循指數衰減
  4. 穩態：電路達到零電流和零電壓

數學基礎

時間常數定義

RL 電路的時間常數定義為：

$$ \tau = \frac{L}{R} $$

物理解釋：

  • 單位：秒（s）
  • 意義：電流衰減到初始值 36.8% 的時間
  • 電路行為：表徵放電速率

電流衰減公式

RL 放電電路中的電流遵循：

$$ i(t) = I_0 e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

其中：

  • ( i(t) )：時間 t 時的電流
  • ( I_0 )：初始電流
  • ( t )：開關打開後的時間
  • ( τ )：時間常數 ( = \frac{L}{R} )

電阻電壓分析

電阻電壓公式

RL 放電期間電阻兩端的電壓為：

$$ V_R(t) = E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

公式組成：

  • ( V_R(t) )：時間 t 時的電阻電壓
  • ( E )：初始電壓（與初始電感電壓相同）
  • ( t )：放電開始後的時間
  • ( τ )：時間常數 ( = \frac{L}{R} )

物理解釋

電阻電壓特性：

  • 初始值：( V_R(0) = E )（最大電壓）
  • 衰減模式：隨時間指數衰減
  • 最終值：( V_R(\infty) = 0 )（穩態時零電壓）
  • 能量消耗：功率在電阻中以熱能形式消耗

時間相關行為

關鍵時間點：

  • t = 0：( V_R(0) = E )（初始電壓的 100%）
  • t = τ：( V_R(\tau) = 0.368E )（初始電壓的 36.8%）
  • t = 2τ：( V_R(2\tau) = 0.135E )（初始電壓的 13.5%）
  • t = 3τ：( V_R(3\tau) = 0.050E )（初始電壓的 5.0%）
  • t = 5τ：( V_R(5\tau) \approx 0 )（實質上為零）

電感電壓分析

電感電壓公式

RL 放電期間電感兩端的電壓為：

$$ V_L(t) = -E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} $$

公式組成：

  • ( V_L(t) )：時間 t 時的電感電壓
  • ( E )：初始電壓大小
  • ( t )：放電開始後的時間
  • ( τ )：時間常數 ( = \frac{L}{R} )
  • 負號：表示與電阻電壓相反的極性

物理解釋

電感電壓特性：

  • 初始值：( V_L(0) = -E )（初始電壓的負值）
  • 衰減模式：大小指數衰減
  • 最終值：( V_L(\infty) = 0 )（穩態時零電壓）
  • 極性：與電阻電壓相反以維持電流流動

極性解釋

為什麼是負號：

  • 楞次定律：電感器反對電流變化
  • 電流方向：放電期間，電流減少
  • 電壓極性：電感器產生電壓以反對電流減少
  • 能量守恆：維持電路平衡

電壓關係分析

基爾霍夫電壓定律驗證

在任何時間 t，迴路中電壓總和必須等於零：

$$ V_L(t) + V_R(t) = 0 $$

代入公式：
$$ -E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} + E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} = 0 $$

這確認了我們的公式滿足 KVL。

電壓大小關係

相等大小：

  • 電阻電壓：( |V_R(t)| = E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )
  • 電感電壓：( |V_L(t)| = E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )
  • 關係：( |V_R(t)| = |V_L(t)| ) 在所有時間

相反極性：

  • 電阻：正電壓降
  • 電感：負電壓降
  • 淨效應：迴路中總電壓為零

能量考量

初始能量儲存

電感器中的磁能：
$$ W_L = \frac{1}{2} L I_0^2 $$

能量消耗

電阻中消耗的功率：
$$ P_R(t) = V_R(t) \cdot i(t) = E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} \cdot I_0 e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} = E I_0 e^{-\frac{2t}{\tau}} $$

總能量消耗

能量守恆：
$$ W_{total} = \int_0^{\infty} P_R(t) dt = \frac{1}{2} L I_0^2 $$

這確認了所有儲存的能量都在電阻中消耗。

與 RL 充電比較

電壓極性比較

元件 充電階段 放電階段
電阻電壓 ( V_R(t) = E(1 - e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}}) ) ( V_R(t) = E e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )
電感電壓 ( V_L(t) = E e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} ) ( V_L(t) = -E e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )

電流方向

  • 充電：電流從 0 增加到 ( I_{\infty} )
  • 放電：電流從 ( I_0 ) 減少到 0
  • 電壓極性：反轉以維持正確的電流方向

實際應用

1. 電力電子

  • DC-DC轉換器：開關電路中的電感放電
  • 電機驅動：磁場繞組放電
  • 逆變器：能量回收系統

2. 保護電路

  • 突波保護：電感能量消耗
  • 斷路器：電弧抑制
  • 緩衝電路：電壓尖峰保護

3. 能量儲存系統

  • 電池管理：電感放電控制
  • 超級電容器系統：能量轉移優化
  • 飛輪系統：動能轉換

數學性質

指數衰減特性

衰減速率：

  • 變化率：( \frac{dV}{dt} = -\frac{E}{\tau} e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )
  • 初始速率：( \frac{dV}{dt}\big|_{t=0} = -\frac{E}{\tau} )
  • 衰減因子：( e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} ) 決定衰減速度

時間常數效應

小時間常數（τ << 1）：

  • 快速放電：電壓快速衰減
  • 高功率：大的初始功率消耗
  • 短持續時間：快速完成暫態

大時間常數（τ >> 1）：

  • 慢速放電：電壓逐漸衰減
  • 低功率：小的功率消耗
  • 長持續時間：延長的暫態期間

範例計算

例題問題

給定：

  • 電感器：L = 100 mH
  • 電阻：R = 50 Ω
  • 初始電流：I₀ = 2 A
  • 初始電壓：E = 100 V

計算：

  1. 時間常數
  2. t = 2τ 時的電阻電壓
  3. t = 2τ 時的電感電壓

解答

1. 時間常數：
$$ \tau = \frac{L}{R} = \frac{100 \times 10^{-3}}{50} = 2 \times 10^{-3} = 2ms $$

2. t = 2τ 時的電阻電壓：
$$ V_R(2\tau) = E \cdot e^{-\frac{2\tau}{\tau}} = 100 \cdot e^{-2} = 100 \cdot 0.135 = 13.5V $$

3. t = 2τ 時的電感電壓：
$$ V_L(2\tau) = -E \cdot e^{-\frac{2\tau}{\tau}} = -100 \cdot e^{-2} = -100 \cdot 0.135 = -13.5V $$

進階分析

非理想元件

實際考量：

  • 電感電阻：內部電阻效應
  • 鐵心損耗：磁滯損耗
  • 溫度效應：元件參數變化

多重時間常數

複雜 RL 網路：

  • 串聯 RL：多個電感器串聯
  • 並聯 RL：多個電感器並聯
  • 混合配置：組合網路

頻域分析

拉普拉斯變換方法：

  • 轉移函數：系統響應分析
  • 極零點分析：穩定性考量
  • 頻率響應：交流行為分析

解題策略

1. 電路分析

  • 識別：電路拓撲和元件
  • 確定：初始條件
  • 計算：時間常數 τ = L/R
  • 應用：適當的電壓公式

2. 公式應用

  • 電阻電壓：( V_R(t) = E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )
  • 電感電壓：( V_L(t) = -E \cdot e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} )
  • 時間點：在特定時間計算
  • 驗證：檢查 KVL 符合性

3. 結果驗證

  • 單位檢查：確保正確的電壓單位
  • 物理合理性：驗證結果合理
  • 定律驗證：確認基爾霍夫定律
  • 能量守恆：檢查能量平衡

常見誤解

誤解一：電壓極性

錯誤：假設電感電壓與電阻電壓具有相同極性
修正：電感電壓具有相反極性以維持電流流動

誤解二：能量損失

錯誤：認為放電期間能量損失
修正：能量守恆，從電感轉移到電阻

誤解三：時間常數

錯誤：混淆充電和放電時間常數
修正：兩個過程使用相同的時間常數 τ = L/R

參考影片

標題： RL放電暫態電阻與電感電壓公式解析 - 張偉勤老師
連結： https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z2NOmVPGAdw

本文發布日期：2025-08-02
